Events of Night of Knives which takes place after the indictment of sorcery on Malaz Isle

1160 - Siege of Pale begins
1161 - Itko Kan massacre, Cotillion possesses Sorry
1162 - The Seventh Closure and events of Midnight Tides

Gardens of the Moon
The Malazan Empire sieges and captures Pale, then fights for control over Darujhistan. The mission was a failure and resulted in the outlawry of the Bridgeburners
Deadhouse Gates
Felisin Tavore breaks out of her enslavement in the Otataral Mines, travels across the continent and becomes Sha’ik, leader of the Rebellion against the Malazans

Fiddler and Kalam want revenge against Empress Laseen for the betrayal against the Bridgeburners and used the excuse of returning Apsalar and Crokus home to go to Seven Cities, where Kalam starts the Rebellion to weaken the Empire. Meanwhile, Fiddler finds the Azath House, Tremorlor, for a secret warp into the heart of the Empire
Coltaine leads a host of refugees across the continent to Aren
Memories of Ice

The outlawry of the Bridgeburners was a ruse between Laseen, Dujek, and Whiskeyjack so they can enter a temporary ceasefire and alliance with Caladan Brood and Anomander Rake to deal with the Pannion Domin
The Genabackan campaign ends
House of Chains
The new untested Malaz 14th Army, led by the newly appointed Adjunct Tavore Paran, is sent to put down the Whirlwind Rebellion
The Whirlwind Rebellion is destroyed by internal conflict and by the Tanno Spiritwalker’s song summoning and ascending the Bridgeburners
Rebel Fist Korbolo Dom had intended to betray Sha’ik and return to the Malazan Empire
Adjunct Tavore slays Sha’ik, without knowing it was her little sister
Karsa Orlong goes on a long journey of ✨
self discovery✨
Midnight Tides

The Letherii Empire slowly encroaches on Tiste Edur territory, conquering and enslaving other tribes nearby. Warlock King Hannan Mosag made a deal with the Crippled God to obtain power to unite the Tiste Edur tribes and defend his people from the Letherii Empire
Sent the Sengar brothers on a mission based on a dream, to travel and retrieve a mottled sword crafted by the Meckros swordsmith Withal
During a fight with the Jheck, Rhulad wielded the mottled sword himself and was cursed by the Crippled God with immortality and the loss of sanity with every death
Rhulad leads the Tiste Edur to conquer Letheras

Hull Beddict loved the tribes he worked with and swore vengeance against the Letherii Empire for exploiting them. Tehol Beddict, with the help of Bugg/Mael, worked to undermine the Letherii economy in revenge for his brother Hull. Brys Beddict served as the King’s personal guard, defeated Rhulad, but dies drinking the same poison as King Diskanar who had no faith in surviving the Tiste Edur conquest

Epilogue
1164, 24 days after Sha’ik was killed
19 year old Sergeant Hellian of the Septarch District on Kartool Island, infested with fist-sized paralt spiders that she hates and so she is always drunk
Corporal Urb is like her sidekick
A strange ship, built in a style more than 50 years old with arcane etchings in the prow, sails into Kartool
It should've been impossible to sail around Kartool due to the Clear Season making it impossible to navigate around the island for the next two months
The Malazan ship sends a local boy to send Sgt. Hellian a message to meet at the grand temple of D’rek

Walking through the dilapidated temples, Hellian remembers times before the Empire came, when fetes were celebrated for the island’s patron goddess D’rek with the Demidrek leading a procession walking barefoot over maggots and worms
Children would chase and stone lame dogs to death while screaming D’rek’s name
Criminals would be thrown into pits to be devoured by carrion beetles and fireworms
Kellanved sent Dancer and Surly to eliminate the D’rek sorcerers, with the help of Tayschrenn, the former Demidrek that the grand temple ousted in an internal coup
After the Malazan conquest, the festival was outlawed, slavery was abolished, execution pits were swept clean, and even had shelters that adopted lame dogs
The Septarch consisted of (7):
D’rek, the Worm of Autumn
Soliel, Lady of Health
Poliel, Queen of Disease
Beru, Lord of Storms
Burn, Lady of the Earth, Elder God
Hood, Lord of Death
Fener, Boar of War
After the conquest, a few more gods were added
Dessembrae, Lord of Tragedy
Togg, Wolf of Winter and War, Elder God
Oponn, the twins of chance
At the grand temple, Hellian finds the one who sent her the message
Banaschar, middle aged man with shoulder length hair wearing Malazan sailor garb and ‘fevered eyes’
Banaschar was a D’rek priest at the Jakatakan temple on Malaz Island, came immediately because he sensed danger in the grand temple
Cpl. Urb notices all the paralt spiders on the steps are dead and decayed
Hellian has her men batter down the grand temple door
Crowds from the other temples gather, and the Queen of Dreams priestess recognizes Banaschar and demands to know why he's here
The door opens revealing a scene of a bloody massacre with no survivors
Sgt. Hellians drinks from her flask inside the temple against Banaschar’s wishes and orders to have the area secured
Banaschar plans to investigate all the temples and disappears via warren
Hellian expects the Fist is gonna punish them
A dozen Nameless Ones carry out a ritual to release Dejim Nebrahl
T’rolbarahl are demonic creations of First Emperor Dessimbelackis, before he created the Hounds, that the Emperor wanted dead because they ate humans and were too smart to manipulate
The last seven t’rolbarahl imparted their souls into a woman widowed by the Trell wars and made into a Mena Mahybe, a vessel, for a child that would host the seven souls and become its d’ivers form
The child was able to escape the T’lan Imass, fed on other soletaken and d’ivers, but was captured and bound by the master of the Deragoth
The ritual used:
Mockra, Path of Mind
Telas, Path of Fire
Denul, Path of Healing
D’riss, Path of Stone
Meanas, Path of Illusion and Shadow
Kurald Emurlahn, Elder Warren of Shadow
Tellann, Elder Warren of Fire
Hood’s Path, Path of Death
Kurald Galain, Elder Warren of Darkness
Rashan, Path of Darkness
Thyrllan, Elder Warren of Light
Starvald Demelain, the First Warren of Dragons and Chaos
Deadhouse Gates
During the era of the First Empire (humans), the Nameless Ones tasked Mappo to be Icarium’s guardian. A Nameless One contacted Mappo during the events of this novel
Revealed later by Gothos that the Nameless Ones slaughtered Mappo’s people and lied to Mappo that it was Icarium’s fault.
The Nameless Ones had staves made of Azath roots and wood. Icarium may have had his memory damaged (along with attempting to destroy an Azath house to free his father Gothos)
Corpses of the Nameless Ones littered the ground around the Tremorlor Azath house
The Nameless Ones resented Kellanved and Dancer for entering the Deadhouse, an Azath house in Malaz City.
Dancer ordered his Talon to assassinate all Nameless Ones in the Malazan Empire
House of Chains
The Ashok Regiment were residing in temple of the Nameless Ones during the Whirlwind Rebellion
The Tanno Cult, which squad mage Ebron is from, is claimed to be a direct descendant of the Nameless Ones
The Nameless Ones had imprisoned a demon that could possess anything that consumes its blood

The Nameless Ones worshipped the Azath and sought the First Throne of the T’lan Imass. Logros moved the First Throne to Quon Tali to avoid the Nameless Ones and was surprised when Kellanved found and took it
Midnight Tides
A Nameless One priestess came to Letheras, traveled with five Nerek witches, and had her soul placed in Kettle’s Body along with a Forkrul Assail soul
Notable things in their chants
Patterns long foreseen reveal their struggles have been for naught
Unmitigated truths are buried underneath the sands of Raraku
The Nameless Ones had taken part in Chaos pursuing this world, and acts to influence another force so that it mutually annihilates the force of chaos
Shadowthrone knows too much about the Azath, a potential enemy to the Nameless Ones
The Nameless Ones believe events of the mortal realm shape the ground that gods walk on
Barghast, Trell, and Tartheno Toblakai all descended from Imass
Frozen worlds hide in darkness, there will come a time when death discovers its own visage
The 12th Nameless One, Sister Spite, makes sure Dejim Nebrahl agrees to their task before freeing him
A force of entropy known as otataral frees Dejim Nebrahl, and he devours the eleven Nameless Ones as he is released
Taralack Veed, a tattooed Gral warrior and last of the Enoth line, camps north of Dejim Nebrahl’s release
He watched a mottled scaled dragon [Sister Spite] fly up, calls her a bitch, and follows Dejim Nebrahl
Veed has a habit of using his spit to slick back his hair
Prologue Scene 3 (Raraku, Taralack Veed)

The village was once renowned across the Seven Cities continent for its lumber used for sarcophagi, farmed into extinction the village had been reduced to 18 villagers, a wayside stop for Malazan travelers on the road
Barathol Mekhar is a taciturn black smith, onyx skinned, the only resident not native to the village and its unofficial leader
[Note: Kalam’s last name is Mekhar]
Barathol recognizes five T’lan Imass approaching and tells the villagers to prepare weapons and hide
Book One:
The Thousand Fingered God
1164 Burn’s Sleep, 58 days after Sha’ik’s death
[Apsalar] enters Ehrlitan and orders rice wine at an inn
The bartender asks if she belongs to Dujek’s Army which had left six days ago, she says she belongs to none
As she walks upstairs to her room, she repels a man by cutting his face with a knife
A simple fishergirl was possessed by Cotillion and Rigga the Seer, a wax witch, before the slaughter of Itko Kan
Rigga the Seer was grieving her family lost in war, foresaw Apsalar’s possession and thus wanted to protect her
Shadowthrone and Cotillion wanted revenge for their deaths, planned to use her for the Empire’s downfall
She enlisted under the name Sorry and was attached to the Bridgeburners
In Darujhistan, the mischievous god Oponn gifted Crokus Younghand a coin which made him a target by several people, including Sorry, who did not want Oponn disrupting any of their plans
Right before attacking Crokus, Anomander Rake threatened Shadowthrone with Dragnipur to stop his schemes in Darujhistan and thus ended Sorry’s possession
Rigga the Seer’s protection kept Sorry’s mind from shattering
Crokus Younghand takes Sorry back to the city and gives her the name Apsalar, after the Lady of Thieves
Crokus was swept up in the events in the Malazan conflicts against Darujhistan.
His uncle Mammot was possessed by the Jaghut Tyrant Raest and was killed
Tasked by Anomander Rake to protect Alchemist Baruk, knocked the assassin Vorcan unconscious with two bricks which saved Baruk’s life
Once the conflict was over, the Bridgeburners (then outlawed) had found Sorry. Realizing she is no longer possessed and feeling pity for her, Kalam and Fiddler decide to take her home to Itko Kan.
Crokus decides to tag along
Fiddler and Kalam found an opportunity to take revenge against Empress Laseen for their annihilation at the Siege of Pale and their outlawry.

Decided to detour to Seven Cities. Kalam would initiate the Whirlwind Rebellion while Fiddler takes Crokus and Apsalar to find the Tremorlor, an Azath House, somewhere on the continent that connects to the Deadhouse, an Azath House in Malaz City.
As a backup plan, they wanted to use Apsalar’s skills gained by Cotillion to have her assassinate Laseen
Fiddler, Crokus, and Apsalar are attacked by soletaken and d’ivers, but are saved by Icarium and Mappo Runt
They are very friendly and take them to Tesem Temple, a temple of Shadow inhabited by Iskaral Pust
Most likely from Shadowthrone and Cotillion’s schemes, Apsalar’s father Rellock had been sent to Iskaral Pust as his servant.

Iskaral made a deal with Rellock, to spare his and Apsalar’s lives and restore his missing arm, in exchange for planting false trails leading the soletaken and d’ivers away from the Path of Hands to be trapped by the Azath House, Tremorlor
Iskaral tried to make Apsalar become Sha’ik Reborn and trap Icarium in Tremorlor, which both failed
The group fought their way to Tremorlor, only Crokus, Apsalar, Rellock, and Fiddler were transported to the Deadhouse in Malaz City
They reunite with Kalam, who had spoken to Empress Laseen and gave up his plan to kill her
Apsalar requests Shadowthrone to take her, her father, and Crokus back to her home in Itko Kan and sever all ties between them and the gods

Apsalar’s father, Rellock, passed away as soon as they returned home to Itko Kan. Cotillion gives them a job to sail to Drift Avalii to confirm if Tiste Edur are attempting to take the Throne of Shadow
On the island, they help Rake’s brother Andarist, Tiste Andii grandchildren, stranded Malazans, and Traveller defend the throne against a Tiste Edur attack
Andarist and the stranded Malazans die, Traveller takes up his sword Vengeance the duty to guard the Throne of Shadow
Cotillion then tasks and transports Crokus and Apsalar to Tesem Temple for a task, yet unspecified
Apsalar bargains with Cotillion to stop making Crokus a killer and leaves to be his servant
Cotillion grants Crokus the duty to be Felisin Younger’s next guardian
Leoman’s army, the last force of the Army of the Apocalypse that still has the Holy Book of Dryjhna, uses a sandstorm as cover to escape Tavore’s pursuing army
Corabb Bhilan Thenu’alas, Leoman’s right hand man, remains faithful and believes in Leoman, who doesn't believe in himself
Leoman of the Flails was a member of the Army of the Apocalypse. He was imprisoned by the Malazans in Ehrlitan and joined Karsa Orlong when his friend Torvald Nom helped them escape
Mebra was the traitor that led to Leoman’s imprisonment
Together, Leoman and Karsa journeyed into the desert and joined Sha’ik (Elder)
Leoman had rescued Corabb Bhilan Thenu’alas from Gral warriors and Corabb had sworn loyalty ever since

Leoman was present when Sha’ik received the Holy Book of Dryjhna and was assassinated immediately by the Red Blades. After watching her body for weeks, Felisin and Heboric arrived, making her the next Sha’ik

After the defeat of Coltaine on the Chain of Dogs, Felisin as Sha’ik retreated the Army of the Apocalypse because she felt she needed the power of Raraku to defeat her sister Tavore and the Malazan Army
Leoman convinced Sha’ik to take 1,500 men and had made several successful attacks against the incoming Malaz 14th Army
The sappers were able to ambush Leoman’s guerilla army with Moranth munitions and reduced their numbers significantly

During the Battle of Raraku, Korbolo Dom betrayed Felisin (Sha’ik), Mathok fled with the Holy Book of Dryjhna to Y’Ghatan and agrees to meet Leoman there, and Felisin challenged Tavore by herself and dies
Leoman is now leading the remnants of the Army of the Apocalypse to make one last stand at Y’Ghatan

Samar Dev was stranded in the plains when she took an investor out to test her invention, a wagon that moves using two levers. The investor died, she broke her foot kicking the wheel out of frustration, and slowly succumbs to dehydration
Karsa Orlong appears, giving her a flask to drink and offers to save her if she can help him enter the city beneath notice to purchase supplies
Karsa Orlong, a hulking man with a shattered slave face tattoo, wearing white bear fur cape, riding a man eating horse that drags two heads of Hounds in his wake. Beneath notice he emphasizes.
Karsa tosses Samar Dev around, not sympathetic for her broken foot that flops around

Karsa Orlong wanted to imitate his grandfather’s legendary raid of the human settlement on Silverlake with his companions Delum Thord and Bairoth Gild. On the way there, they free the Forkrul Assail named Calm. At Silverlake, the humans were able to kill his companions and imprison Karsa by Silgar
Karsa Orlong befriends Torvald Nom who manage to escape, but Karsa Orlong stays to kill as many humans as much as he can. Eventually he is subdued by the Ashok Regiment who also captured Torvald.
The Ashok Regiment sends Karsa, Torvald, and his Nathii slavemasters to the otataral island

While sailing to sailing to the Isle, Karsa’s prayers to Urugal sends the ship to the Nascent. Karsa and Torvald explore the Nascent, slaughtering the crew of the Silanda, fighting black catfish, until they reunite with the Nathii slavemaster who has the sorcery to transport them back to the mortal realm
Karsa and Torvald land on the Seven Cities coast by the otataral sea where they spend time with Keeper who has a tower with a huge skeleton of a K’Chain Che’Malle

Karsa and Torvald travel south to Ehrlitan, but slavemaster Silgar managed to hire local tribes to enslave them both again. Torvald lights a fire that attracts the attention of a dangerous tribe, Gral, which gets him killed and Silgar transports himself and Karsa through warrens and ends up in Ehrlitan
In Ehrlitan, Silgar claims Karsa is his slave, but are both arrested by Malazans because he doesn’t have the sanctioned slave brand. Karsa receives the shattered face tattoo.
Karsa escapes with his cellmate Leoman, a leader of the Army of the Apocalypse and Torvald’s help with the Gral attacking the Malazan compound
Silgar manages to convince the Malazans he’s on their side and pursue Karsa, but Karsa defeats them
Leoman takes Karsa to Sha’ik and they become her protectors

Several years later and Sha’ik (Elder) is assassinated by the Red Blades the moment Kalam Mekhar delivers the Holy Book of Dryjhna. Felisin Paran and Heboric manage to reach them after escaping the otataral isle and she becomes Sha’ik

Leoman is tasked to take the desert warriors and scout the Malaz 14th Army’s position. Karsa prays to the Seven Faces who want him to travel westward to free them, and also where he’ll find a Jhag horse to fight alongside Leoman against the Malazan army

Karsa leaves Raraku, runs into Mappo and Icarium, finds a barrow where his ghost companions of Delum and Bairoth take him into Tellann to fast travel to the Jhag Odhan, freeing the Jaghut Aramala when he finds her in the warren

Karsa finds the flint weapon cache where the Seven Faces wanted him to and the Unbound are now free. Karsa makes a flint weapon for himself, and then rebel against his former gods. On his journey, Karsa realized the Teblor were slaves to the Unbound who did nothing in return for them
Returns to Raraku with Siballe’s skull
Upon returning to Raraku, he slays Bidithal, Febryl, Silgar, and two Deragoth
Having grown from the boy he once was, he announces to Adjunct Tavore that the Malazans are no longer his enemy
As a mercy, Karsa throws Siballe’s skull into the Raraku Sea to grant her oblivion and swears to be the leader his people deserve to follow
Apsalar wept in her room for abandoning Crokus, feeling undeserving of his love and not wanting him to follow her path
Cotillion also told her Crokus is traveling with two women, which she believed would help him move on quicker
Apsalar goes downstairs to pay for her lunch and two nights for her room
Two Pardu women flank her and says their Gral wants Apsalar to dance for him, she declines and states she’s a ‘Shadow Dancer’ which scares everyone off
The bartender recognizes Apsalar as coming from Itko Kan, himself being a former soldier of Dassem Ultor’s army and missed Y’Ghatan because of a spear wound to his back
Apsalar leaves the inn, enters an alley, slips into the Shadow warren, and sees the mortal realm through a filter
The Pardu women trailed her lose track of her and say they should inform their new master
Apsalar followed a path, ended up in a square with walls lined with shackles, two of which held Tiste bodies
Telorast and Curdle, ghosts possessing the bodies, speak to her in the Tiste Andii language
The duo planned to break into Shadowkeep, but ran into the Hound Baran and ended up shackled by a seven headed demon lord
Cotillion had previously come to taunt them
The duo offer to be Apsalar’s companions and guard her dead body unto eternity, unless it's against Edgewalker, Shadowthrone, Cotillion, or an aptorian
Apsalar agrees to escort them to a gate that might as well be Hood’s gate, and they have to leave their bodies behind
Leoman’s army made camp for the night around a water well in a dried out lake basin
Leoman walks Corabb away from camp to speak
Corabb finds and enthusiastically eats a hallucinogenic toad
Despite Leoman’s pessimism, Corabb has faith in him and in Dryjhna as he increasingly gets high and has hallucinating thoughts involving feathers
Corabb returns to camp alone, Leoman’s thoughts on Karsa and being compared to a meer-rat (impossible to catch, hiding in any sized hole with its hinged skull)
Karsa is denied entry into Ugarat because of the Hound heads
Karsa dismounts, sets down Samar Dev, and tosses the gate guard into a cart, KO’ing him
This is fine he says, he wants an inn with a stable
Karsa gingerly places Samar Dev back on Havok, watching for her broken foot, and she leads them down the street threatening curses to those around them
Samar Dev admits she's a witch but bargains with spirits and does not bind, because ‘One who binds risks getting bound in return’
That made Karsa silent and thoughtful
Captain Inashan and guards appear to arrest Karsa, who then wields his flint sword
Samar Dev intervenes, spinning a story that Karsa was a wild land spirit she called upon to save her. The Hound heads are trophies of demons that would've attacked Ugarat
Karsa cuts through the lie, as he does, and announces himself as Toblakai, the once bodyguard to Sha’ik
Samar Dev attempts to cut Karsa off, but he answers honestly in that the Malazans have won and best to make peace with them, and not wise to follow Leoman’s path
Karsa even offers to make peace with a Malazan garrison holding out across the river
Inashan says he’ll send a healer for Samar Dev and leaves
Samar Dev:
Toblakai, how have you survived this long in Seven Cities?
Karsa:
There is no armour made that can withstand the truth
Samar Dev:
When backed by that sword?
Karsa:
Yes, Samar Dev. I find it did not take long for children to understand that.
Apsalar tell Telorast and Curdle her name, the duo claimed to know her as Imass and that Telorast stole from her temple coffers to earn her anger
Curdle claims they were mages, necromancers, spiritwalkers, conjurerers, wielders of fell Holds, and mistresses of the Thousand Warrens
Apsalar exits the Shadow warren, along with Telorast and Curdle in their ghost forms
Telorast and Curdle want bodies to possess
Throws out names of creratures from Starvald Demelain: imbrukes, stantars, luthuras
Telorast and Curdle have been speaking in Tiste Andii because they assumed it was Apsalar’s native language
Apsalar orders the duo to stay back as she goes to assassinate her target, or else she'll tell Cotillion and send the Hounds after them
As Apsalar travels to a dome temple to find her target, she thinks on the duo’s imprisonment
The Shadow warren does not have its own Azath house
All features in the warren - menhirs, tumuli, trees, stone walls, boulders - had chains shackled to a prisoner
One stone circle has three dragons chained to it
The assassination was more for Shadowthrone’s revenge, whom they think will be at the center of the next convergence
Apsalar studied her possible routes, wrapped a telaba scarf around her head, mand entered into a fissure entrance where she found her target, Mebra, killed almost right before she arrived

[Note: In Deadhouse Gates Mebra was tasked by the Red Blades (Seven Cities natives loyal to Laseen) to give Kalam the Holy Book of Dryjhna to deliver to Shai'k which allowed the Red Blades to find and assassinate immediately after the book was delivered.]
[Note: In House of Chains, Leoman and Karsa had just escaped imprisonment in Ehrlitan when they ran into Mebra who snitched to the Malazans]
A Semk assassin attempts to kill Apsalar with throwing stars and a poisoned, broad and hooked kethra knife
The Semk made a downward cross slash and thrust with the knife and struck Apsalar’s hip with his right hand
Apsalar dodges right and  stabs through his ribs into his heart, killing him
Cutting his clothes revealed tattoos written in First Empire language, he is a priest of the Nameless Ones
Telorast and Curdle discuss
How pretty Apsalar is are
How they need to stick with her or Edgewalker will be unhappy with them
How they're going to try to cheat them all
How they want their ‘throne’ back
Shadowthrone fidgets on the... Throne of Shadow in Shadowkeep as he watched Iskaral Pust murmur to himself, having decided Iskaral Pust is enough to do a job and sends him away
Current form is wispy shadows with eyes of haematite (black crystal)
Cotillion doesn't think he'll ‘get there in time’ or is ‘sufficient’
Shadowthrone decides to go for a walk outside Shadowkeep
The shadow warren shifts landscapes when one is not looking
Currently has forested hills to one side, ravines/gullies in between, and a ghostly lake on the other side
Artorallah demons sailed their dozen ships to raid coastal Aptorian villages
Shadowthrone could command them but did not want to test their loyalty, too busy with his own schemes
Cotillion walked the broken trail down into a gully, then up the slope that reaches a plateau that had a ring of standing stones as if a detonation tilted the stones like a petal of a flower
Edgewalker appeared next to Cotillion, trailed by Baran
The Hounds could track Edgewalker who seems to make fun that Shadowthrone and Cotillion can't do the same, even calling them usurpers
Edgewalker won't tell Cotillion want he wants, but will follow Cotillion to see what he says to three dragons chained at the standing stones,‘There is no privacy in Shadow’

Edgewalker says the standing stones are always half buried. The ones in the Shadow Warren are the underworld counterpart. The overworld manifestation may exist as inward tilting stones if they haven't eroded yet
The dragons are Ampelos, Kalse, and Eloth
Cotillion believes in the coming years, there will be a war that draws upon all ascendants from every realm and want to have the dragons on his side
The dragons tried to take the Throne of Shadow, but the Tiste Andii are insistent that the Throne remain vacant, the dragons were chained by Anomander Rake
The dragons hint that Shadowthrone is sitting on a false throne, that the true Throne isn't in the fragment of Emurlahn they currently exist in
Cotillion hints Shadowthrone may not be either and smiles, making the dragons speechless and piques Edgewalker’s interest
The dragons reveal that they helped K’rul shape the flavour of his blood to create the warrens
Eloth was the Mistress of Illusion - Meanas, Mockra, and Thyr
Ampelas shaped the paths of Emurlahn which the Tiste Edur use
Kalse keeps his a secret
Cotillion asks about Soletaken dragons like Anomander Rake and Scabandari Bloodeye
The dragons are surprised Cotillion knows of Scabandari, whose soul remains alive and tortured. The one who shattered his skull [Note: Kilmandaros] is not loyal to the dragons
Cotillion asks further, naming Olar Ethil and Draconus
Edgewalker reveals the dragons wanted the Throne of Shadow to heal Emurlahn, a noble cause
Cotillion hints he doesn't care about that, but who sits on the Throne after
Cotillion recounts what he knows

The dragons helped K’rul shape his blood to create warrens and become the sources of sorcery, and then were supposed to return home to Starvald Demelain because if the dragons interfered or were active across realms, magic would be unpredictable and feed Chaos, the eternal enemy
[Note: As of right now, Chaos is known as a force that wars with Darkness. Not elaborated further, it just sort of is there, may or may not be important by the end of the Kharkanas trilogy]
However, the Soletaken have Tiam’s blood and could freely travel. Each race had their own eleint
Tiste Edur, Scabandari Bloodeye whom the dragons accused of murdering the Edur royal line, spilled blood in the heart of Emurlahn, and opened the first fatal wound on Emurlahn
Tiste Andii, Anomander Rake
Tiste Liosan, Osserc
T’lan Imass, Olar Ethil whom brought Thyr to her people
Draconus is a mystery
Some of the Soletaken and dragons had the same sorcery, incase a dragon died
Elder Gods are not of one world
When Darkness ruled alone until the coming of light, there were elemental forces moving unseen
Cotillion asks if the Crippled God is an Elder God and wants to know how to kill one so the Crippled God could stop poisoning the warrens
‘A sundered realm is the weakest of them all! Why do you think the Crippled God is working through it?’
And thus Cotillion successfully manipulated the true goal from this conversation and leaves
Edgewalker is impressed and offers his assistance, considering himself to be an ‘elemental force’, an Elder God in other words
The Crippled God assaults the First Throne of the T’lan Imass and the Throne of Shadow
Cotillion and Shadowthrone are alone and need allies
Can't trust the Hounds because the Edur, who are loyal to the Crippled God, has mastery over them

[MoI Prologue] 119,739 years before Burn’s Sleep (the current year in HoC is 1164), eight Jacuruku mages rebelled against their tyrant, Kallor, by dragging a god into their realm. The god’s shattered body rained down on the continent killing the mages, and nothing to Kallor himself
The Crippled God became insane and wanted to spread suffering to everyone in the world
Various gods gathered to chain the Crippled God to Burn’s flesh so he would not escape or basically destroy the world. Was repeated several times.

The Crippled God poisoned Burn’s flesh through his chains, poisoned the warrens, created the House of Chains sanctioned by Master of the Deck Ganoes Paran (Gruntle convinced him that the Crippled God could be forced to follow his rules and limitations)
Burn is the elder goddess of the earth. She sleeps in the core of the world, her pain causes earthquakes and the world ends if she wakes up
Burn created a hammer and entrusted the decision to Caladan Brood
Using the hammer would break the Crippled God’s chains. Waking Burn would kill all life, but at least the world gets reborn
Not using the hammer, the Crippled God would eventually kill Burn. Everyone dies, no reborn world
At the end of Memories of Ice, he recruited Gethol (former Herald of Hood, a Jaghut and brother of Gothos) to be his Herald and Kallor as High King
L’oric reveals the first jade giant, aliens from another world, was found chained by otataral in the otataral mines
The Seven Faces in the Rock, the gods of the Teblor, are actually seven T’lan Imass that failed in destroying the Jaghut, Aramala, and was entombed in the Laederon Plateau as punishment
The Crippled God gave them the power of the Chaos warren in exchange for their loyalty
After guiding Karsa to the cache of ancient T’lan Imass weapons, the Unbound achieved their freedom and left to assist the Tiste Edur in supporting the Crippled God
The Warlock King, Hannan Mosag, planned to use the Crippled God’s power (and betray him) to amass power to defend themselves from the Lether Empire
However, Rhulad Sengar instead took on the Crippled God’s cursed sword forged by the Meckros swordsmith, Withal
With the Crippled God’s guidance and immortality, Rhulad Sengar was able to lead the Tiste Edur and conquer the Lether Empire
Icarium plays and splashes around in the newly flooded Raraku sea

[Note: Fiddler had saved the grandchildren of a Tanno Spiritwalker in Ehrlitan. When the Spiritwalker touched Fiddler’s shoulder, he enacted a powerful magic in the form of a song that would activate when Fiddler returned to Raraku, the region that formed the Bridgeburners. When Fiddler arrived at Raraku with Tavore’s army, the song triggered unleashing the Tanno Spiritwalker magic, ascending the Bridgeburners, and the Raraku desert remembered it had once been a sea and flooded itself]
Mappo turned over slabs of dolomite, revealing complete skeletons of Jaghut children killed during the wars between Jaghut and T’lan Imass
Dolomite is soft and a good surface to crave glyphs, erodes slower than limestone, absorbs power that still lingered to imprison the Jaghut children
The Imass were enslaved by Jaghut Tyrants, thus commited to a vengeful genocide against all Jaghut
Crystal metaphor

‘He had seen crystals growing up in a single night from the desert floor, facet after facet revealed like the petals of an opening flower, and it seemed to him that brutality behaved in a like manner.’
‘Icarium. My crystal’
Imass and Jaghut war. ‘And so the crystal grew, facet after facet.. Until this.’ [This being the dolomite tombs]
Icarium recalls some memories sparked by the flood
Cities that are long gone: N’karaphal, Trebur, Inath’an Merusin (present day Mersin), Hedori Kwil, Tramara
An era when the First Empire was already declining
Icarium is determined to travel to the ruins of Trebur, the Domed City, 15-16 days’ travel from their current location
A days’ travel west of the Mersin River
Mappo and Icarium had made this trip before 80 years ago, though Icarium didn't have these memories back then
Mappo Runt had traveled with Icarium for over 200 years, keeping watch over him and making sure Icarium does not recover his memories and keep his rage in check.

While traveling the Pan’potsun Odhan, they get involved with the Path of Hands (something that would allow the victorious soletaken or d’ivers to ascend) and discover its gate within Tesem, a Temple of Shadow with Iskaral Pust as its priest
Mappo and Icarium join Crokus, Apsalar, and Rellock in diverting the soletaken and d’ivers away from the Path of Hands, instead into to be funneled and trapped into the Azath House, Tremorlor
After entering the House, Mappo and Icarium are transported to Aren Way after the Army of the Apocalypse defeated and crucified the Chain of Dogs
Mappo rescues the Hengese lap dog Roach and Wickan cattle dog Bent
Icarium forgets the entire sequence of Deadhouse Gates and they wander off westward into the Jhag Odhan
Mappo and Icarium met Karsa Orlong when he left Raraku to find a Jhag Horse for himself
Icarium was excavating a cave containing a statue of a seven-headed hound
Karsa faintly recognized Icarium’s names in the caves of the Laederon Plateau and Icarium recognized Karsa as Teblor, calling his tribes fallen
Icarium shatters Karsa’s ironwood sword, Karsa punches Icarium’s face KO’ing him, and Mappo bonks Karsa with his club KO’ing him

Mappo Runt’s elders performed a ritual which summoned the Nameless Ones. Mappo is named as a ‘chosen warrior’ to be Icarium’s guardian. They told him that Icarium had destroyed his home village that became a trader town
The Nameless Ones were the left hand of the First Empire (human), with another sect being the right hand
When entering the maze of roots that led to Tremorlor, corpses of the Nameless Ones littered the floor
Icarium has memories of the Nameless Ones telling him he should never travel alone, and remembers various faces of different partners throughout history. The Nameless Ones make him lose his memory
Dancer and Kellanved has ordered the Talon to kill all Nameless Ones because they resented them for entering the Azath Deadhouse in Malaz City
Gothos, Icarium’s father, reveals to Mappo that the Nameless Ones had destroyed Mappo’s home, not Icarium
On a trail in the Path’Apur mountains, a week since the group left Pan’potsun
Crokus (aka Cutter) was tasked by Cotillion to protect Felisin Younger. Thus he travels with her, Scillara, Heboric, and Greyfrog
Their current goal is to sail to Otataral Isle so Heboric can return ‘something’
After a delightful conversation with Greyfrog, who ate a wasp nest, Crokus goes to find Heboric while he is searching for a spring water source with the help of the land’s spirits
Heboric is a Destriant of Treach, with tiger markings on his body, and ghostly claws at the end of both his stumps
They return to ask Greyfrog questions, and Crokus being concerned he might eat the two girls
Scillara was nervous around Greyfrog while Felisin Younger played with him as with a dog
She was the only one Greyfrog does not speak to telepathically
Scillara feels more clear minded now that she's no longer smoking durhang, she is also healthier and stronger from their travels
Scillara wonders what she's going to do with the baby she's pregnant with, perhaps sell it
The baby was either Korbolo Dom’s or one of his men
Four highwaymen the group crossed the day before appears and approach the women, Scillara planned to sleep with them so they wouldn't be harmed
Greyfrog immediately leaps and bites the head off one man with his unhinged jaw
The second man, Greyfrog used two arms to grab both of the man’s arm popping his elbows, a third arm to crush his neck, and the fourth arm to scratch his own back (LOL)
The third man, Greyfrog leaps to punch and cave in his skull
The fourth man, Greyfrog pulls him away from his horse and bites his head off
Heboric and Crokus return
Greyfrog shares his excitement to Crokus that he's obtained horses
Heboric warns the horses really don't like Greyfrog
‘Confident. They just don't know me yet.’

Koryk and Smiles get into a petty argument, Smiles throws a knife into Koryk’s leg, Bottle comes to heal the wound and return the knife, Smiles throws it again between Koryk’s legs, Corporal Tarr takes and keeps the knife for now
The Malaz 14th Army, led by Adjunct Tavore Paran, feels robbed of fighting the Army of the Apocalypse themselves, chasing after them through the plains
Mostly picking fights with themselves
It's been ten days since the rumor started that the 14th Army is getting new recruits and captains which they sorely need
Now that Keneb is promoted from Captain to Fist after Fist Gamet’s death, the 14th Army had no official captains
Bottle takes a locust and feeds his scorpion, Joyful Union
Bottle misses his grandma, and thinks on the Eres’al that haunts his dreams and shows him visions of stone had aces across the land
[Note: Bottle had picked up an axe head and sensed Eres’al’s presence before the Army of the Apocalypse had fallen Chapter 24 Scene 2]
The sapper Cuttle appears and brought karybral fruit
Fiddler and Kalam find a spot under three guldindha trees to eat and drink ale in private
Kalam noticed more gray in Fiddler’s russet beard and pale blue eyes looking faded
Thought how Fiddler and Hedge were best friends and how he saw the ghosts of the Bridgeburners during the downfall of the Army of the Apocalypse at Raraku
Kalam mentions the Claw Pearl and Red Blade Lostara Yil hover close by, likely so Empress Laseen can keep an eye on Tavore
Fiddler feels that Tavore is untested, especially now that Fist Gamet is dead
[Note: Tavore’s only battle experience so far was fending off Leoman’s raider on their way to Raraku. Her 14th Army did not actually fight at the Battle of Raraku]
Quick Ben appears via imperial warren
Tavore sent Grub [Note: Fist Keneb’s adopted toddler son] as a messenger to arrange secret meetings before Pearl gets to eavesdrop, hiding in his own warren.
Tavore who didn’t wear her otataral sword out of courtesy.
Tavore wants her own cadre of assassins, unknown to the Claw
Kalam says Tavore is strong, unpopular but that can be achieved when they eliminate Leoman’s army
Fiddler shares Cuttle’s concern that they’ll all be ‘wearing Ranal’ by the time they finish off Leoman’s army

[Note: When chasing Leoman’s army in a sandstorm, Corabb blindly ran into Fiddler and got tangled in his munitions, resulting in detonating the entire bag which killed Lt. Ranal and splashed his blood all over Cuttle. Cuttle then tells his superiors, ‘I’m wearing Ranal’]
Cuttle says he’s been sitting on a cusser he’s been holding back until ‘when the doom descends on us all’
High Fist Dujek Onearm, High Mage Tayschrenn, along with a Seti with a waxed mustache [Hattar] and a middle-aged woman with short brown hair and a heart shaped face [Kiska] appear via imperial warren
Quick Ben tells Kalam that Tayschrenn’s role has been misunderstood and tried to protect Whiskeyjack, but was too late
Quick Ben refers to Tayschrenn as a High Mage colleague, Tayschrenn retorts that field promotion hasn’t been sanctioned by the Empress yet
Quick Ben reveals that High Mage Kribalah Rule the Rude of the Blackdog campaign was actually him all along, so technically he does have a High Mage title
Quick Ben, as High Mage Rule, had saved Tayschrenn’s life from Tiste Andii assassin-mages
Tayschrenn was disadvantaged because he missing an object to summon a demon lord. The same one that Quick Ben used to escape Anomander Rake in Darujhistan
Dujek Onearm says he’d clap if he still had two hands, and reins them in to have their discussion
Pearl and Lostara Yil spy on Dujek’s meeting, thinking he should be in G’danisban right now
Lostara Yil leaves because of the chigger fleas, Pearl can easily cast a cantrip to get rid of them but just.. doesn’t
Telorast convinces Curdle to possess something more animated than Apsalar’s used chamber pot as Apsalar climbs out the window
While on the roof, Apsalar thinks about how she first came to Ehrlitan with Crokus, Kalam, and Quick Ben
Also thinks about Mebra, the Nameless Ones, the targets on her assassination list, and what she will do after
Cotillion appears, sitting on the roof next to her
Apsalar reports about Mebra’s death and how he was aiming to be a High Mage
Telorast and Curdle are agents of Edgewalker
Cotillion met Edgewalker the first time he ascended [Note: Night of Knives], Edgewalker has some curiosity about Apsalar
Apsalar touches, near caresses Cotillion’s jaw
Cotillion freezes but they both stop and move on
Apsalar wants to detour the coastline before her next target
Cotillion warns her about Telorast and Curdle, jokes they employ the same tactic as Iskaral Pust of confusing others
Apsalar and the ghosts return to her room at sunrise
The ghosts complaining that a sun exists in this world and hides in the shadows, lest they disappear
Apsalar travels to the caravan camps outside the city walls to track the merchant whose Gral and Pardu women guards were interested in her being a Shadow Dancer
She stalks two Red Blade guards to avoid their notice
The merchants are happy and thriving with the war being over and Malazan rule has returned
Apsalar sits down to eat tapu (skewered fruit and meat) and finds the Gral and Pardu guards arguing over a cage of puppies
Satisfied, Apsalar returns to her inn room to take care of another task
Upon returning, the ghosts reports that a big, black, hairy, fanged and clawed, boot-wearing demon appeared via warren trying to look for Apsalar
Apsalar wakes up two hours past sunset and heads to the Jen’rahb with Telorast and Curdle
A shadowy manifestation of a stone and mortar causeway, shaped like an aqueduct, stretches from the base of Apsalar’s inn window to the Jen’rahb
It appeared about a minute before Apsalar woke up
Below the city of Ehrlitan faded into rubbles of ruin
In the distance, ghostly towers above a shadowy city, a domed palace, a lake with ships
Nearby were bridges over canals, Tiste Edur were seen crossing them
Below was a dead body that was not Tiste Edur
Telorast and Curdle sensed a throne
Apsalar and the ghosts arrive at Jen’rahb, the shadow manifestations disappear behind her
Mebra was stripped naked, his living quarters were thoroughly scoured by someone either looking or hiding something
Curdle comes to warn Apsalar that someone’s coming
Apsalar hides beside the entrance and waits for both Pardu women to enter
Apsalar stabs the first woman's elbow and KO’d the second with the knife pommel to the head 😵
Apsalar kicks the first’s head and punches her chest knocking her to the ground
Apsalar removes all the weapons from the second, then goes over to the first, breaks her elbow, and choke slams her into the wall
Telorast and Curdle argue who gets to possess the KO’d second woman, Apsalar chooses Curdle
The Pardu woman admits their boss is Karpolan Demesand, a merchant of the Trygalle Trade Guild
The crew is resting, returning from their last jobs which were making deliveries to Coltaine on the Chain of Dogs and delivering altar stones to Y’Ghatan
Karpolan Demesand wanted to buy information from Mebra
As a peace offering to Karpolan Demesand, Apsalar tells them Mebra was killed by a Nameless One
Apsalar KO’s her with her knife pommel 😵
Curdle tells Apsalar of the tablets hidden in a secret cache under the floor
An excavated pit with sacks of soft clay, bone scribers, and tablets
One tablet wrote about a grand Rashan meeting, two of whom are Apsalar’s assassination targets
Bridthok of G’danisban
Rival and leans on his relative Bidithal
Septhune Anabhin of Omari
A follower aka sheep(?)
Sradal Purthu of Y’Ghatan
A dangerous fool
Torahaval Delat of Karashimesh
A bitch, not funny or dangerous like her cousin
[Note: Quick Ben’s full name is Ben Adaephon Delat]
Several tablets about lists of contacts, detailed notes on how to extort people
Another tablet wrote that Mebra’s aide, Sribin, confirmed that Taralack Veed, a most secret dagger of the Nameless Ones, was in Ehrlitan in the past month
A Khundryl wanderer told the tale of a barrow and a dragon
‘Dessimbelackis [First Emperor] curse the Nameless Ones’
Another tablet recording events that happened in [Note: Deadhouse Gates]
Duiker freed Heboric, Kalam going to Sha’ik whom the Red Blades planned to kill
Apsalar and the ghosts leave before the Pardu women wake up
The ghosts pretend they didn’t say anything about a throne
The Holy Falah’d (ruler) of Ugarat stands with 50 men outside the Moraval Keep, where Karsa planned to walk in and meet the besieged Malazans
The keep was carved into a flat mesa
Karsa tells Havok not to eat anyone and simply walks in
Karsa climbs into the moat, piles on large rocks for a makeshift stairs up to iron double doors which bashed open with his blade
The Falah’d of Ugarat is frightened and wants to get Karsa out of the city
Karsa enters Moraval Keep, chutes for boiling oil and slits for arrows pointed at the entrance
Past the gate was a courtyard with the sky above was open
The keep was like four walled city complex
22 stories in the back wall, 18 stories to the left, 17 stories to the right, and the front wall had 12 center stories flanked by projections with 6 stories each
There was a gaping pit in the courtyard with a ladder that led to an underground beehive tomb, no doors, with a dais
Two sets of three thick iron spikes submerged and looking like they imprisoned something
The Malazans used it as a latrine pit
A reptilian beast attacked Karsa

Stands on two legs, long arms with talons, stunted and thick tail, broad snout with rows of dagger long fangs, flaring cheekbones and brow ridges, deep set eyes, serrated crest that bisected the elongated skull, pale yellow green hide
The beast grabs Karsa with its talon and pulls him out of the tomb, flinging him across the courtyard into a wall
The beast charges at Karsa and is taken by surprise when Karsa charges right back
Karsa gets real close into the beast’s space, headbutts the underside of its jaw, shoulder tackles its belly and he wraps his arms around its right leg to lift it up
Karsa plants his right foot behind the beast’s left foot and pushes, breaking the beast’s right leg
The beast tail whips Karsa into the air and falls down into the sewage of the tomb
Tomb of Agamemnon
A beehive tomb in Mycenae, Greece built in the Bronze Age ~1250 BC
Karsa climbed out of the pit, the reptilian beast was gone
Karsa guessed it stayed inside the keep and explored deeper into a chamber
Karsa dodges the beast’s surprise talon attack, running through a doorway, blindly tripping over a divan chair, crushing a low table, and rolling further onto carpet
Karsa dodges to the side and blocks the beast’s jump attack with a massive chair, making it dive into the floor
Karsa kicks it throat and the beast kicks Karsa across the chamber into a wall
Karsa charged at the beast, grabbing its right wrist, then spinning like an alligator to pop the beast’s arm from its socket
Karsa climbs onto its back and hammer pounds its skull until it was crushed
The beast fell to its side, pinning Karsa
Karsa wraps around its neck, but the beast pulls Karsa off and throws him at the crushed low table
Karsa takes a table leg and swings, parrying the beast’s arm
Karsa charges and gets kicked in the chest, getting knocked out
Karsa wakes up, hearing a crashing sound above him, and limps through a side door
The Holy Falah’d wonders if Karsa is negotiating with the Malazans and expresses his doubts to Captain Inashan that Karsa is Sha’ik’s Toblakai, thinks he’s either looting or raping someone inside
Samar Dev says the Keep has been completely explored, no loot to be found any more
Karsa follows the reptilian beast down the hallway, the beast turns around and attacks
Karsa knocks way the beast’s hand, knees its belly, then uses his thumb to stab into the beast’s left arm to grab and tear away ligaments and muscle
The beast slumps over Karsa and slices off a flap of Karsa’s skin on his head
The beats falls to the ground over Karsa
Karsa dodges out of the way and pounds the head until it’s flattened and dead, blood and fluids leaking out ☠
Karsa walks over to a side chamber where he picks up a wine jug from a table, lays on the floor, stares up at a mural of gods with mocking expressions painted on the ceiling, then drinks the wine
The sun is setting as Captain Inashan is getting soldier ready to enter
Karsa exits the Moraval Keep, covered in blood and shit, saying the Malazans gone and nothing important happened
A week had passed, Leoman’s Army of the Apocalypse are 4-5 days away from Y’Ghatan to stand siege of the Malazans
The city Kayhum is visible to the south
Corabb recalls an embarrassing memory and eats a slug with roe
Corabb believes Dassem Ultor, the Malazan Empire’s First Sword had died there, but Leoman believes he’s alive
[Night of Knives: Dassem Ultor survived Laseen’s assassination attempt in Y’Ghatan and escaped with Temper and Ferrule. Current whereabouts unknown.]
Leoman wants Corabb to ask him who Dassem Ultor is
Corabb instead thinks about how great Leoman is, how it’s a tragedy that Leoman wasn’t given the opportunity to lead the rebellion, and mutters ‘Blessed Dessembrae hounds our heels…’
Leoman is impressed and says Dassem Ultor is Dessembrae, the Lord of Tragedy. A reluctant living god, like Anomander Rake, that eternally wanders and hunting for something
Leoman wants to make a last stand at Y’Ghatan to spite and curse the Malazans
Leoman has a burden he keeps secret and doesn’t hold Corabb’s promise to stay with him
Corabb tells Leoman of the olives, merchants, and Vedor, the Holy Falah’d of Y’Ghatan
Corabb has indigestion
Bottle thinks the Army of the Apocalypse is headed to Y’Ghatan
Sgt. Fiddler/Strings announces they’re taking a break and has Cuttle start a fire and make food
Soldiers mentioned by name
Bottle, Strings, Koryk, Smiles, Tarr, Roach, Bent, Cuttle, Flashwit, Uru Hela, Neffarias Bredd
Smiles said she saw Neffarias Bredd a couple days ago
Fiddler speaks with Bottle in private, knows Bottle can spy on others in the camp with his lizards and asks what he’s heard
Bottle hasn’t heard much around the Adjunct, mentions Pearl, Tayschrenn, Quick Ben, Nil, and Nether (but not really much about them)
Fiddler thinks Bottle can access more warrens than Quick Ben
Bottle’s grandmother taught him how to use Holds, like Hood and Shadow. He doesn’t like warrens
Fiddler wants Bottle to meet Quick Ben, Bottle is scared that QB might notice the Eres’al following him
As Fiddler and Bottle head to Nil & Nether who’s casting a ritual, Bottle asks about Gesler’s squad
Gesler’s squad is escorting Kalam and Quick Ben ahead, Bottle advises they shouldn’t go by warren ‘just because’ and doesn’t elaborate further
Nil and Nether are in a ring of stones, Spiritwalking like the Tanno Spiritwalkers
Fiddler asked why Bottle joined the army
Bottle’s grandmother thought it was a good idea. She passed away, her spirit was restless
Bottle was selling dolls that would appease Stormriders to sailors in the Jakatakan ports
Fiddler feels cold, Bottle knows the twins are in Hood’s gate looking for the Wickans that died in the Chain of Dogs
Bottle feels something is wrong and jumps into the ring of stones, vanishing
Bottle enters Hood’s warren, onto a floor, ankle deep with rotting bones and a grey sky overhead
Nil and Nether stand next to a screaming lich that grabs and tosses them before leaving, it was their mother who wanted them to stop moping, grow up, and for Nether to take a husband and get pregnant
Nil can tell Bottle ‘rides life-sparks’ the way the twins did when they were children
[Note: The twins are reincarnated warlocks]
Bult approaches with a dozen dogs, telling the twins ‘We do not belong here’ and for Nether to get pregnant and have babies
Nether doesn’t understand why they’re so adamant, Bottle suggests to repopulate the Wickan tribe which pisses her off
Bottle exits the warren and flees with Fiddler before Nether wakes up
Bottle sends a lizard to know what curse Nether’s going to cast on him so he could counter it
Kalam, Quick Ben, Gesler, Stormy, Truth, Pella, and Sands are tasked by Adjunct Tavore to reach Y’Ghatan before Leoman’s Army of the Apocalypse and are thus traveling via imperial warren
Several massive shapes appear behind them
Apart of the ‘Old Guard’ that served during Kellanved’s reign. Served as coastal guard near Hissar during Deadhouse Gates. Followers of Fener, the Boar of War.

When Hissar was attacked by the Whirlwind Rebellion, they joined imperial historian Duiker and mage Kulp to flee on the ship, the Ripath, and sail to the otataral mines to rescue exiled historian Heboric.
On the otataral coast, they found Felisin, Heboric, and Baudin who just escaped the Skullcup mines after the uprising. An unnamed insane mage dragged them to the Nascent
The group of eight explore the Nascent and find the Silanda, find the remains of the Tiste Edur Karsa Orlong slaughtered during his time spent in the Nascent
Six Logros T’lan Imass appear, they are pursuing renegade kin (The Seven Faces in the Rock)
When Karsa harpooned the tiste edur mage, he died midcast so his warren stayed open and became a wound
Legana Breed gives Stormy his flint sword, and sacrifices himself to close the warren wound
Kulp used his Meanas (illusion) warren to find an undead dragon, ‘The Unwelcome’, and drags the Silanda in its wake to escape
The dragon takes the ship through the Meanas warren, and then the Tellann warren of fire which made Gesler, Stormy, and Truth ascend, tempering their skin to bronze
The Silanda lands with only the coastal guard trio near Vathar Crossing and intersect with Coltaine’s Chain of Dogs
Captain Lull promotes them, Gesler teases that he’ll punch him and pull Coltaine’s thong. Coltaine laughs and punches his metal faces, breaking his own hand
The trio take all the wounded from the Chain of Dogs on the Silanda and sail to Aren
After the slaughter outside Aren, the old guard trio look for Duiker’s body and rescue the dogs Roach and Bent
At Aren, Gesler is appointed Sergeant in the 8th Legion of the Malaz 14th Army (Tavore’s)
In his squad was Corporal Stormy, Truth, Pella (soldier and first contact at the Skullcup mines that helped Felisin escape), Sands (sapper), Tavos Pond (Meanas mage)
Lostara Yil and Pearl went to Gesler to ask about Felisin’s last known location
Took part in the scorpion fights while tracking the Army of the Apocalypse
After the battle of Raraku, the Tiste Liosan approached the group and Gesler had Sands shoot a cusser to scare them away
The Tiste Liosan reveals (to the reader) that Gesler, Stormy, and Truth ascended when they passed through not only Tellann, but also Kurald Thyrllan
Happened when the dragon [Olar Ethil] pulled the Silanda to escape the Nascent
Mappo mulls over his role to deceive Icarium and keep his rage in check as long as he possibly can, until he inevitably fails. He feels shame

When Mappo and Icarium come across strange chasms on the plains, out of simple curiosity they descend a third of a league down and discover a lake of melted Omtose Phellack ice, which he describes as ‘dead’
Mappo has magical pouches which shrinks with each pouch. He stuffs his backpack in 3 layers of pouches
Icarium swims down to examine a near pristine mechanism, which he did not build, underwater as Mappo sets up camp
Mappo recognizes basalt that was an intruder to the bedrock and figures they are in a skykeep
According to the Nameless Ones, the K’Chain Che’Malle had invaded the world with the skykeeps far before the First Empire existed
Possible defenders were the Jaghut, Forkrul Assail, or even the Elder Gods
Icarium discovered a corpse of a reptilian beast that resembled a K’Chain Che’Malle with a stubby tail. It was in the pilot seat in reach of levers
Icarium concludes a Jaghut had sealed the mechanism in ice
Mappo and Icarium explore the skykeep further, Icarium sensing excitement in Mappo after being so forlorn for so long

cards.h: *** K’Chain Che’Malle and K’Chain Nah’ruk (MoI, MT)

i.html: The K’Chain Che’Malle are one of the four Founding Races. They are very intelligent dinosaurs that developed technology and whose Kaschan warren manipulated gravity
The K’Chain Che’Malle ruled the Letherii continent. When Scabandari Bloodeye shattered Kurald Emurlahn, he led his people to invade and seek refuge in the mortal world and slaughtered the KCCM

Passed down through every generation of the Sengar women, the K’Chain Che’Malle performed a Kaschan Ritual as vengeance against the Tiste, turning Mother Dark into a black hole and set up the heat death of the universe
The last KCCM city was Morn (Southern Genabackis), where the ‘Short-Tails’ were about to rebel

In Kallor’s Empire, his researchers studied ancient barrows and constructs. KCCM Matrons came together to resurrect the primitive Short-Tailed ancestors, but they refused to work together and engaged in civil war which led to the destruction of their race
As a consequence, a rent that led to Chaos was opened and a Matron sacrificed herself to seal it
The Pannion Domin had read in Gothos’ Folly that the K’Chain Nah’ruk, the Short-Tails, were the ones that created the flying fortress, and believes Moon’s Spawn is a K’Chain Nah’ruk skykeep

The Queen of Dreams, Goddess of Divinations, was a god reflected in several cultures, no single group could claim her as their own
Leoman laughs, saying ‘Desire and necessity’ of the Cold Dream
Leoman asks Corabb to reaffirm his loyalty, as Leoman wants to talk to the Queen of Dreams herself
Mappo and Icarium believe that the Tiste Edur are responsible for killing the dragon Sorrit
The K’Chain Che’Malle are innocent, possibly even ignorant of Sorrit’s death
First Fener, now Sorrit
Sorrit was spiked with otataral onto Blackwood, sourced from Tiste Edur forests from the Shadow warren
The Shadow warren wanders and respects no boundaries and thus manifests in two places at once
Mappo explains the sanctity of spilled blood

Blood is the sacred life force, the soul’s own stream. Spilled blood has power. Blood can be absorbed, and can be tainted by fear and pain. The soul can sense its own demise, stress, and become poisoned
Sorrit was murdered in the Shadow warren and drawn to here. Its spilled blood and the otataral spikes overwhelmed the Omtose Phellack sorcery, melting its ice
Icarium recognizes the Jaghut that cast Omtose Phellack here and wishes to travel to the Jhag Odhan to speak to her
Icarium regains a few fragments of terrible memories, realizes Mappo must be protecting the world from Icarium
[Note: Possibly Phyrlis and Aramala]
The Malaz 14th Army has arrived outside Y’Ghatan, a half hour’s walk south of the city walls
The sixteen barrows dedicated to Dassem Ultor, his First Sword, and other Malazans were open. The rebels had dug a sewage trench that emptied and defiled the corpses here
The Y’Ghatan civilians are seen traveling westward [Note: That Leoman ordered to Lothal]
Fist Keneb observed Bent’s disfigured cattle-dog body, Roach the lapdog being a menace by pissing on his shoes
Fist Temul, leader of the Wickans and has grown almost two feet since leaving Aren, resembles Coltaine more and more in behavior
Temul suggests attacking at night to distract the enemy, so the sappers can approach and use Moranth munitions to knock down a wall or two
Fist Keneb and Warleader Gall feel nervous, feeling that Leoman is going all out to make one final stand and murder as many Malazans as he can
Leoman would’ve escaped if he kept traveling west where the Malazans can't catch him
Admiral Nok is sailing to Lothal and High Fist Dujek will be in his way after capturing another city
‘The first casualty among the defeated is recalling their own list of crimes, Fist’ - Temul
Grub has been hanging around Temul often, his uncanny statements seem to have an effect on Temul
Temul freezes when asked what he would do in Leoman’s place
Temul rejects comparison to Coltaine, feeling shame that he was sent away on the Chain of Dogs
Roach looks like he’s chewing on a Malazan bone
Bottle is telling all the sergeants Cpt. Faradan Sort wants to meet with her company at dusk at the sheep pen south of the road
Bottle walks over to Sgt. Balm’s 9th Squad
Corporal Deadsmell, Throatslitter, and Widdershins were playing a game of Troughs. Tossing black stones and rolling in a cup
Galt and Lobe were arguing over whose herbs to boil
Balm is of mixing paint to make death masks
Bottle moves on to Sgt. Moak sitting by himself. His cooking made his whole squad have diarrhea
Sgt. Moak placed a bet with Fiddler about something, don't know what it is yet
Bottle moves on to Sgt. Mosel whose squad is dismantling a wagon
Flashwit, Mayfly, Taffo, Uru Hela
Mosel and Mayfly said they heard from Smiles that Neffarias Bredd was nearby, as big as a Fenn
Sgt. Sobelone and Sgt. Tugg’s squads are betting on a wrestling match
Saltlick bit Shortnose’s ear off (who is also missing the tip of his nose)
Shortnose’s wife as of last week, Hanno. is betting against him
Toles, Corporal Reem
Bottle walks off to the graveyard to find Sgt. Balm dancing in a looter’s pit
Balm lists off the curses for interrupting his Dal Honese death dirge, stops when Bottle threatens to make a doll out him
Bottle returns to Sgt. Fiddler’s squad, hoping Fiddler and Cuttle finished fixing Moranth munitions to their crossbows while he was delivering Cpt. Faradan’s message
Sgt. Gesler comes and wants to talk to Fiddler about Quick Ben, Kalam, and Stormy’s mission later
Gesler wants to avoid meeting Captain Faradan Sort
Cpt. Kindly is with some other company that needs ‘pulling into shape’
Gesler wonders why not not send Claws into to deal with Leoman instead
Cuttle shares a rumor from Sgt. Hellian that Laseen’s gathered the Claw around her close and tight. Veteran companies on Quon Tali were sent to Unta and Malaz Island
Sgt. Hellian’s a drunk, but they seem to trust Cpl. Urb as capable
Bottle walks to the meeting place and finds a rubbish mound full of foundation stones, shattered idols, animal bones, broken pottery
Black glazed Malazan style pottery depicting Dassem Ultor’s death outside Y’Ghatan, the Empress on her throne, the First Heroes and the Quon Pantheon
The local style of pottery was more elegant. White glaze on the necks and rims. Faded red on the body. Full toned and realistic images.
Bottle picks up a local style shard depicting Coltaine's crucifixion with crows overhead, dead Wickans and Malazans below him, an impaled cattle dog
Bottle drops the shard when a whispered chill goes down his spine
Carrion birds, capemoths, and rhizan flying overhead, Bottle took that as an omen
Moving further south of the meeting place, older red pottery shards depicting chariots, figures on stilts wearing ornate headdresses and hooked weapons
Bottle’s philosophical musings on what is worth going to war
The old have their ambitions, the young with their eager mindless zeal and attempts for companionship
Boredom was a poor reason to fight, better to wield the brand of righteousness no matter how misguided or lacking in subtlety
Bottle hears his grandmother’s voice and advice, but is starting to suspect it's not her
She had lived through the pre-Empire days on Quon Tali. The Itko Kan-Cawn Por wars. Untan Confederacy. Li Heng League.
Emperor Kellanved ended all of the conflicts, killed all the tyrants, and ended their distant wars
Bottle summons lizards, rhizan, and a hoof-sized spider to spy on Cpt. Faradan Sort’s meeting with the sergeants
Suddenly, Bottle sees the Eres’al approach and that they're in a savannah, an ancient memory of the landscape
Ape like, brown fur, human face, heavy breasted, pregnant
The Eres’al followed the Malaz 14th Army, not knowing what she was following. As if both worlds existed in the same moment, and there’s no back to return to
The Eres’al threw sand and barked at Bottle, then placed his hand on her pregnant belly
Bottle sensed something. That the spirit in her belly was an answer to a distant abomination, the corruption of a once-innocent spirit
The father was Tiste Edur, not human, an intruder from another realm bereft of innocence
[Note: Trull Sengar. When Monok Ochem opens an Eres bone pile gate to transport Trull Sengar and Onrack to the First Throne, an Eres Witch appeared and stole Trull’s seed.]
The Eres'al was chosen because she is the last innocent ancestor of humans before the species degrades
The child was the only pure candidate for a new Throne of Shadow to command a healed realm
The Eres'al prayed to Bottle. Bottle did not want to be her god, she shakes him, teeth bared, and pins him to the ground and about to pummel him with her fists
Bottle relents and accepts being her god
Bottle returns to his world
Fist Keneb meets with Adjunct Tavore Paran
Fist Tene Baralta, the Red Blace, shows her a map of Y’Ghatan drawn after Dassem Ultor’s death
One age of construction remained resilient, thus a maze of pockets, old rooms, half buried streets, and corridors still stand underneath Y’Ghatan
Fist Blistig is worried why Leoman sent all of his civilians away and doesn't know what Leoman is going to do with Y’Ghatan
Adjunct Tavore has given orders to Cpt. Faradan Sort and dismisses Blistig and Tene Baralta
Tavore tells Keneb that Dujek’s Host is broken and will never be the same, its soldiers are randoms picked up from previous Genabackan campaigns
Dujek’s Host retains its façade of being a powerful force that gives morale to Malazans and makes the enemies cautious
However, the Malaz 14th Army is the last great imperial army
Dujek’s Host being the reinforcement is the only hope they have going into Y’Ghatan
Tavore needs to crush Leoman before Dujek’s 2nd Army is exposes its inexperience and weakness
Tavore tells Keneb because she knows the soldiers respect him more than her, leaves the decision of revealing the truth to Keneb
Keneb heads to the sergeants’ meeting
Keneb confronts Fiddler about whether or not Tavore is right about Dujek’s current condition
Keneb can’t ask Quick Ben, who was at Coral with Dujek’s army, so he wants Fiddler to validate Tavore
Fiddler responds ‘I misjudged the Adjunct. She's better at reading signs than I thought’
Fiddler knew
Paran’s carrack vessel sails into Kansu’s harbor
Ganoes Paran says he was treated well enough by the Bridgeburner survivors
Picker, Antsy, Blend, Mallet, and others in K’rul’s Bar
Paran says he's felt less easy about Elder Gods ever since K’rul was heavily involved against the Pannion Domin
Paran feels suspicion about the Elder Gods opposing the Crippled God
Paran doesn't know if he's an ascendent

Apsalar explains he's harder to kill. That he has power of a personal nature that will draw other powers to him. His perception and thoughts become different. Other people will take notice of him in a bad way
Apsalar tells him there's two lands more dangerous than the others, Seven Cities is one of them
Advises he has someone else fight for him, some people don't play by the rules, and bargain from strength or not at all
Paran thanks her and walks away
Apsalar leave with the ghosts
Telorast and Curdle think if Paran told her what the ghosts really were, she would've destroyed them
Apsalar and Paran walk into Kansu’s harbor
Four of six piers were destroyed by Admiral Nok a month prior
The port city is almost empty because of a plague that broke out of Ehrlitan a week ago
Apsalar associated it to Poliel, Mistress of Pestilence
Neither Paran nor Apsalar have to worry though
All of the healers and priests st their D’rek temple were slaughtered
Apsalar and Paran bid each other farewell, happy they were able to meet
Paran feels they'll meet again
Apsalar likes the feeling of having friends, but doesn't want to get too close or feel vulnerable
Samar Dev and Karsa continue their journey to the Jhag Odhan
Samar Dev begins talking about how magic stifles the need for invention, the way complacency stifles innovation
Karsa retorts she can never be satisfied, instead remains miserable
Karsa makes several leaps of logic
Progress → [relentless ambition] → [by any means necessary] → slavery
Samar Dev and Karsa reach the summit of a limestone ridge, a gorge beyond, more jagged rocks everywhere
A twisted ancient tree at the summit
Karsa senses a beast was here, both of them sense that the spirits have fled
Kalam rock climbs up a K’Chain Nah’ruk skykeep and reaches a ledge just as Quick Ben’s buff wears off
Kalam looks down and sees a black chasm owned where Quick Ben and Stormy were supposed to wait
Kalam calls out to Cotillion and the god appears, eating an apple
Cotillion confirms the skykeep is filled with K’Chain Che'Malle and helps Kalam down to the floor
Cotillion is surprised to hear that Stormy and Gesler got promoted
Cotillion holds a rope as Kalam descends into the chasm
All of the walls had painted figures of humanoids with arms upraised in transcendence, faces filled with joy. At their feet were painted bloody dismembered body parts and mangled flesh
Stormy’s legs are broken and Quick Ben appears unscathed
Kalam slaps Quick Ben awake
Kalam is surprised that QB can use healing magic, QB would rather just let Mallet do it all and Cotillion work on Stormy
Cotillion descends and only realigns Stormy’s legs
Cotillion senses that Stormy has passed through Thyrllan, Kurald Liosan, and/or Tellann. His body healed itself of its broken ribs, liver, hip, and skull
Mentions he's more boring than Urko, who at least had interesting useless hobbies
[Note: the fossil building]
Cotillion guesses the paintings mark the chasm as temples to an Elder God. Either Kilmandaros, Grizzin Farl, or K’rul
Cotillion leaves
Crokus’ group are camped by an ancient tree
Greyfrog, Felisin Younger, and Heboric sense danger and get ready to flee
Mappo and Icarium pass through several caves used as refuge, storage, paintings, and funeral ceramics on the escarpment dating to the First Empire
At the summit, Icarium entered a notched channel carved by rainfall. Mappo followed after him into the stepped walled channel
[Dejim Nebrahl] attacked Mappo and swarmed Icarium in its d’ivers form of multiple t'rohlbarahl
Mappo punches one of them as a second chokes Mappo from behind. A third claws across his chest
Mappo jumped back against the wall, crushing the t’rohlbarahl on his back. Then he grabbed the one in front him him and crushes its head in his hands
Icarium collapses under the swarm
Mappo stumbled forward and falls off the cliff, dragging one of the t’rohlbarahl with him
