Paran hands over his otataral sword to Karpolan Demesand as payment for his contract
The Pardu bodyguards shatter the sword into pieces and Paran collects a shard the size of his index finger
Ganath plans to head westward towards a K’Chain Che’Malle skykeep and bids Paran farewell
Paran travels through the valley, basin, and hills reaching Dujek Onearm’s encampment outside G’danisban where he gets arrested on suspicion for desertion
Paran is taken to Cpt. Sweetcreek’s, a Falari princess, command tent where she immediately assumes he a prisoner and orders him to be executed in the morning
Paran KO’s both Cpt. Sweetcreek and a soldier named Futhgar and ties them up
Paran walks Dujek's command tent where Outrider Hurlochel, formerly of Caladan Brood’s group, recognizes and greets him
The Malaz 5th Army, aka Onearm’s Host, is full of new soldiers picked up from Pale, Genabaris, and Nathilog
Poliel’s plague had come out of her grand temple in G’danisban, from the goddess herself
Onearm’s Host attempted to strike the grand temple with the Hold Moranth but the attack failed
All of the veteran companies and Gold Moranth came back sick, and the healers are losing against the plague
Paran wants to pretend he's still dead, Outrider Hurlochel suggests he impersonate Cpt. Kindly because he's an angry boogeyman amongst soldiers
Lostara Yil walked together with Cpt. Faradan Sort
Doesn't know if Sinn can contact the Malaz 14th Army, or the extent of her power because she is untrained
Cpt. Faradan Sorts admits to being on the Stormwall, that no one is permitted to leave service
Despite being a veteran, believes everything is up to luck and Oponn
Lostara Yil answers she did not survive because of Oponn
[Note: Another god, Cotillion]
Kalam remembers the Black Dog campaign against the Mott Irregulars, Nathii army, and the Crimson Guard
A brutal culling of the Bridgeburners in a nightmarish war
Bogs, lagoons, muddy waters
Quick Ben wonders why Kalam hasn't got revenge on Pearl for backstabbing him
Kalam keeps him around because he wants to find out why Empress Laseen is still spying on Adjunct Tavore
Quick Ben wonder whose side is she on for the war of the gods
Apsalar shares Ganoes Paran is involved as Master of the Deck and has come to Seven Cities
Too many unknown forces, Elder Gods, and Elder Races are involved
Warns Quick Ben that he might not know what the ‘ultimate stakes’ are
Quick Ben wants Pearl gone, very rare for him to openly say something like that
Fiddler carries the Y’Ghatan refugee girl as he hangs back and speaks with Corabb, whom he added to his squad
Clarifies that Malazans do not spear babies as a rite of passage into the army
Reveals Leoman had escaped with a Malazan woman, Dunsparrow
Fiddler freaks tf out to Kalam and Quick Ben, Dunsparrow is Whiskeyjack's younger step-sister. Should be about 25 years old now
Whiskeyjack's stepmom died giving birth, the town elders gave Dunsparrow to Hood’s temple who blessed her in Hood’s name
Their father died, Whiskeyjack was busy with his apprenticeship as a stone mason
Whiskeyjack and Fiddler had to break into the temple and steal Dunsparrow. Attempted to laugh off Hood’s blessing. Fiddler was like an uncle to her.
Fiddler mentions needing a Deck of Dragon
[Continuity Error]
In Memories of Ice, Whiskeyjack tells Anomander Rake how the Bridgeburners were formed and how he met Fiddler for the first time and gave him his name.
Here, however, Fiddler makes it sound like they were friends before they even became soldiers, when Whiskeyjack was still apprenticing as a stone-mason.
Dunsparrow is not important and never shows up again in the entire series. Her name pops up only once in Book 7, and not even directly about her lmao.
Kalam and Quick Ben both slap Sgt. Fiddler for suggesting the Deck of Dragons
Apsalar thinks about Whiskeyjack
Was a stonemason, stone masons are big for divination and symbolism of impermanence and the illusion impermanence
Many Houses in the Deck of Dragons has a mason role
Hood perhaps guided Whiskeyjack into a killer
Dassem Ultor was Hood’s Mortal Sword, perhaps they shared the same cult
Whiskeyjack never seemed religious
Dunsparrow possibly also belonged to Hood. Her presence in the Queen of Dreams means she and Hood are either allies, or Hood is about to ambush her
Apsalar doesn't know whose side Kalam and Quick Ben will choose, might even have to fight them
Also expects Telorast and Curdle to betray her too at some point
Bottle carries Y’Ghatan and the rats while others carry the orphaned children
Koryk has a bowl of bones, he gives one to Cpl. Tarr
Sgt. Fiddler not been introduced to Quick Ben yet
Bottle wonders if the Bridgeburners were forged in Raraku, was Y’Ghatan too much for the soldiers and did it break them instead?
Bottle sees Telorast and Curdle, wonder which mage uses Hood to bind them
Smiles is jealous that Lostara Yil still has all her hair
The soldiers are all suspicious of Apsalar

cards.h: Scene 8, 9, 10, 11 (To Sotka, Hellian, Gesler, Masan Giliani, Fiddler)

i.html: Sgt. Hellian hates the clarity of being sober
Phobia of insects comes out, possibly withdrawal symptoms
Randomly says she wants revenge against Banaschar
The soldiers wrapped their thin clothes around them, sunburnt. Some people have tans on their faces, necks, and hands that scarily contrasts with the rest of their pale body
Sgt. Gesler’s golden skin was unable to be sunburnt
The healers Lutes and Deadsmell were dealing with the blisters
Sgt. Gesler goes to Sgt. Fiddler and suggests sending Apsalar ahead to stop the Malaz 14th Army
But with the possibility they won't believe Apsalar, a stranger, they decide to send Masan Gilani from Sgt. Urb’s squad instead
Meet Masan Gilani, the tall Dal Honese woman with elongated almond shaped eyes. The most beautiful woman in this series [Note: yes I'm thirsty shut up]
Sgt. Gesler tells her the plan, Masan Gilani takes Apsalar’s horse and borrows her kethra knife
Sgt. Fiddler suggests waiting, but Cpt. Faradan Sort only allows a short rest before continue marching
Dejim Nebrahl was compelled by the geas that summoned him to revisit cities that no longer exist.
Yadeth Garath, the first human city with caves still containing Imass bones. Kanarbar Belid. Vithan Taur. Minikenar.
After the battle with Iskaral Pust, Dejim Nebrahl attacked and eaten an entire fisher village, but it wasn't enough for him. He passed by several settlements hit with Poliel’s plague
It grows more fevered and weak without food
Dejim Nebrahl senses a beast and a human, approaches it
Masan Gilani rides in the night time, missing riding horses at home on the Dal Honese plains
All Dal Honese adults can leave the village and live the life of a wanderer, eventually returning home
Children, like Masan Gilani’s two kids, were raised by everyone in the village
When the Malazan Empire conquered Dal Hon, fewer adults traveled, instead younger Dal Honese boys and girls wandered and brought home mixed children
Dejim Nebrahl had one t'rohlbarahl form attack Masan Gilani and the other four feast on Apsalar’s horse
Masan Gilani somersaulted backwards off the horse, and slashed the kethra knife across the t'rohlbarahl’s front legs, pushing it away
She charges and plunged the knife into its neck, killing it ☠
[Four remaining]
Masan Gilani runs, then dives for the second t'rohlbarahl to leap over her and slashes and cripples its back leg
She throws the knife which slices open the t'rohlbarahl’s shoulder and falls somewhere past it
She dashes and jumps over the t'rohlbarahl after the knife, gets raked across her left thigh, and lands on a slope of stones
She climbs the slope whole flinging back sand and gravel
She cuts the back of her hand down to the bone by the kethra knife and grabs it
The t'rohlbarahl tried to jump after her but slides down the sandy and gravelly slope
Masan Gilani climbs up, reaching a ledge and runs
She hears the howls of several Hounds of Shadow. One of them climbs down next to her, looks at her with its amber eyes, then dashes away towards the t'rohlbarahl
Masan Gilani is shocked the Hound is as big as a horse and lies flat on her back to rest
Dejim Nebrahl is appalled that a mere human was able to kill one of them and cripple another, and now is being stalked and toyed with by a hunter it does not recognize
It's hoping its hunter doesn't have as much endurance and will tire itself out, leaving it vulnerable for Dejim Nebrahl
Sgt. Fiddler and the rest of the soldiers are resting in a ditch
Kalam and Quick Ben sense something is nearby, Apsalar only answers cryptically ‘Part of a bargain’

[Note: The Nameless Ones had summoned Dejim Nebrahl to get rid of Mappo and replace him with Taralack Veed. Ganoes Paran bargained with Shadowthrone to send the Hounds of Shadow out of the Shadow warren, so the Deragoth he freed would find and reunite with them. Ultimately Paran’s bargain was to hunt and kill the Dejim Nebrahl]
Sgt. Fiddler looks back and sees Corabb wielding a thick guldindha tree root like a club
Bottle possessed a rhizan and saw the shapes of the Hounds and Dejim Nebrahl, but was too weak to maintain concentration
He also possessed a capemoth to sense that the creatures are coming closer, but thinks they don't care about the Malazans
Dejim Nebrahl had three t'rohlbarahl on the main road while the fourth, one that Masan Gilani crippled, limped far behind them
The Deragoth appears and crunches on the t'rohlbarahl’s necks. One of them managed to claw off one of the Deragoth’s eyes.
The Deragoth kill the three t'rohlbarahl ☠☠☠
Three Hounds of Shadow appear grab the last t'rohlbarahl in its mouth, running away with it
Dejim Nebrahl assume the Hounds have a master that want it still alive
Kalam and Quick Ben are just in shock they saw lizard cats and bear-dogs [Deragoth] that Karsa had killed during the Battle of Raraku
Lt. Pores was recovering from an ambush on his patrol squad
A crossbow quarrel through his arm and sword slash above his knee
Cpt. Kindly drags Lt. Pores off the wagon bed onto the ground, tells him to quit being a bitch and go back to work [Note: what an asshole]
Nearby was a conversation between the Malaz 14th Army’s leaders
Adjunct Tavore, Nil and Nether, Fist Blistig, Fist Keneb, Fist Temul, and T’amber
Nearby was Warleader Gall, Gall’s aide Imrahl, Cpt. Ruthan Gudd, and Cpt. Madan’Tul Rada
[Note: Madan'tul Rada was Lt. to Cpt. Faradan Sort before she deserted to rescue the Malazans stuck in Y’Ghatan]
Cpt. Ruthan Gudd was saying how T’lan Imass had melted Jaghut ice which causes the sea levels to rise. It flooded and sank an island with a citadel near the Malaz 14th Army’s current location
The Falari Isles were midway between Quon Tali and Seven Cities, facilitating trade between the continents
Ruthan Gudd was from Strike Island [Eastern and most isolated of the Falari Isles], claims the Strike people were the original inhabitants of the Falari Isles
Claimed the red and gold haired people who are known today as the typical Falari were actually invaders from some unknown eastern lands across Seeker’s Deep ocean
The old maps had Strike names, none of them were titled ‘Falar’
[Note: Interesting but trivial worldbuilding detail]
The Malaz 14th Army went around Sotka and are now 13 leagues west of the city, by the Kokakal Sea
Fist Keneb hopes they're going to get home ships to return home, and maybe even repair his marriage with Sev
The market stalls had native vendors selling reliquaries of their former enemies in the Chain of Dogs which upset Keneb
Fist Temul still had a faction of old Wickan Crow Clan warriors that never had faith in the teenage commander
Fist Tene Baralta had healed from his injuries, but his mental is still broken
Nil and Nether think Poliel is hunting the Malazans, doesn't matter how many Seven Cities people die along the way
The warlocks don't understand why the goddess hates them
Cpt. Faradan’s Sort’s company reaches Apsalar’s dead horse
Telorast and Curdle are snatching up and eating rhizan, bird sized insects
Apsalar explains to Lostara Yil that they're spirits bound to skeletons
Masan Gilani sits on the slope, her leg still bleeding and tells them what happened
Apsalar lets her keep the kethra knife
Cpt. Faradan Sort orders Deadsmell to go heal her
Bottle walks up and senses Deadsmell using Denul and Hood’s warren, he’s a necromancer
Bottle tells Sgt. Fiddler that Telorast and Curdle are dragons
L’oric and the villagers are trying their best to convince Scillara to raise her baby, she adamantly rejects it
An older villager, Hayrith, says they're a bunch of idiots, that there are two women in the village that would love to take care of Scillara’s baby
She thinks L’oric is going to report to the world that Barathol Mekhar is alive, and Barathol will be hunted down for Aren being slaughtered by the T’lan Imass
Barathol plans to help Crokus’ group reach the coast
L’oric leaves the room, not being able to understand why Scillara doesn't want the baby
Barathol kicks everyone out of the room to talk to Scillara alone
Barathol confirms his involvement in Aren
Scillara tells him he should dig up Heboric’s corpse because Crokus isn't leaving him behind
Barathol leaves to the grave sites, has another villager dig up Heboric’s corpse
Walks over to Greyfrog’s corpse. Flies all died in a circle around it
A smaller Greyfrog emerges from the corpse and makes a scary joke to break the tension. He senses L’oric
Barathol, the villager carrying Heboric’s corpse, and Greyfrog walk back to the village
L’oric and Greyfrog speak to Scillara before departing
Greyfrog has been silent to her because he believes pregnant women should be safe from irritants, but assures he has undying love for her
L’oric attempts one last time to convince Scillara to keep the baby, Greyfrog doesn't share the sentiment but understands L’oric had issues with his absentee father
Scillara affirms she's going to leave the baby in the village for free, without selling it
Plans to continue traveling with Crokus
Crokus quickly recalls his entire plotline in the series until now in only about 60 words
He's in a room with tree trunks on the ceiling, two lamps, empty shelves. He is not awake yet.
He suddenly finds himself witnessing a conversation between the Queen of Dreams, Leoman, and Dunsparrow
Queen of Dreams. Fair skinned. Blonde hair tied up in a mass of braids. Sitting at the edge of a pool with her hand it
Reveals Corabb was a chosen of Oponn, beloved of the Lady (Good luck). QoD was disappointed he did not come
Reveals Dunsparrow is still marked by Hood, that Hood was involved in Whiskeyjack's death for revenge in kidnapping Dunsparrow but regrets it
If Whiskeyjack let Mallet heal his leg injured during the fight with Raest, then the age-old curse would've been broken
Leoman demands to know what the Queens of Dream wants with them. She answers nothing yet
The Queen of Dream smiles at Crokus and he wakes up

[Note: This the Queen of Dream’s only appearance in the main series. She shows up several times as a minor character in the ICE novels. Leoman becomes a minor character in the ICE novels. This is Dunsparrow’s final appearance in any Malazan novel.]
Crokus wakes up for real this time and is greeted by Barathol
Barathol reveals he's a distant cousin the Kalam, the Mekhar tribe was slaughtered by the Falah’d of Aren. Barathol is way bigger than Kalam, and might be issues with him
Barathol tells Crokus about Scillara and the baby, then leaves the room
L’oric thinks about how the village was once a thriving lumber community, but their greed turned their forests into deserts and ruined itself
Thinks about Barathol’s crime in a way that makes a little more sense, but still missing some crucial details for the reader

Barathol was a Red Blade officer that murdered the Fist of Aren. The Red Blades arrested and beat Barathol for staining their loyalty to the Malazan Empire and planned to crucify him. The Red Blades had become even more zealous as an organization because of Barathol

[Note: The Aren Rebellion is never fully explained. We never find out why Barathol killed that Fist of Aren. Neither Erikson or ICE cared to explore the event fully amongst their own worldbuilding, so this is an annoying flaw in the series I don’t like. The Aren Rebellion has no further significance in the series.]
The people of Aren rebelled and drove the Red Blades out of the city, the T’lan Imass had put down the rebellion
Barathol opened the north gate when he left, but the T’lan Imass can move as dust anywhere and don't need no doors open for them
L’oric thinks about how the villagers worship Barathol even after knowing what he did
L’oric struggles to amass his own followers, and shares his frustrations to Greyfrog that he has a hard time keeping himself from imposing his own morality on others
Greyfrog shares the tale of the Silent God, who never spoke to any mortals or intervened in mortal affairs
A cult rose up and chose the Silent God as their deity to commit murders and horrific crimes in his name
Seven great warriors from seven clans set out and found that the Silent God had died the very first time blood was spilled in its name

‘The existence of many gods conveys true complexity of mortal life. Conversely, the assertion of but one god leads to a denial of complexity, and encourages the need to make the world simple. Not the fault of the god, but a crime committed by its believers.’
Gods can be weakened and killed from crimes committed in its name
L’oric and Greyfrog leave the village
[Note: This is L’oric and Greyfrog’s final appearance in the main series. L’oric appears as a minor character in one ICE novel. Greyfrog never appears again]
Villager Filiad tells Barathol that L’oric and Greyfrog left via warren
Barathol is at his smithy, forging something that he spent the last of his money he took from Aren’s hoard
A weapon to use against the T’lan Imass
Boatfinder leads Samar Dev and Karsa on a trail across a landscape of bedrock with trees and clearwater lakes
Samar Dev already thinking of inventing soles that would lessen the impact of footsteps
A dip in the trail led to a fallen tree, revealing its roots ensnaring a corpse missing its head above its jaw, its chest imploded
Samar Dev observed that the corpse’s bones continued to grow into roots
Boatfinder observes the tree is 30 generations old, uprooted and fallen only a week ago
[Note: This is a Jaghut corpse that never gets identified]
Karsa smells something ahead and moves quickly. The group arrive at the Anibar camp by a boggy lake, all of its citizens dead
Boatfinder wailed for his dead kin
Karsa identifies the tracks of the murderers as a large creature with scaled feet
Also, people who came by boat wielding spears and curved swords, moccasins of sewn strips overlapping to create ridges, which made the shoes have better grip. The invaders kidnapped a child
The scaled creature appears, Karsa lunges after it
Samar Dev freezes, clutching a dagger tightly
Boatfinder rocks back and forth on the ground, frightened
Karsa does not want to use the canoes because that would mean abandoning Havok
Samar Dev doesn't think they'll catch up to the invaders, thinks the Anibar are better off moving elsewhere
Karsa believes the invaders are searching, not fleeing
Karsa feels this area has the most omens he's ever experienced
Hawks circling over them, owls watching them
The moon appears large, crumbling, and has a corona glow
[Note: Moon detail #2]
Karsa mentions the desert folk believe the gods wage war up there
Samar Dev disagrees, that the moon is the world’s last child, that it controls the ebb and flow of the tides
Karsa says he could see more ‘fireswords’ at sunrise slashing in the night
[Note: Actual fire swords? Shooting stars? Rays of sunlight? I have no clue]
Karsa says he will return to the Teblor and change their way of thinking, to ask his father for forgiveness and say that he was right
Karsa mentions the Nathii settlement that have enslaved the Teblor, Karsa needs his people to help break their chains and free them
Samar Dev compares Karsa’s Teblor people to the Anibar, living in simplicity and ignorance, justifying their rejection of civilization
Karsa retorts, to Samar Dev’s dismay, with civilization seeking more efficient ways to kill, degrade, and humiliate people
Boatfinder says Iskar Jarak gave them secrets to prepare themselves [against civilized invaders]
Karsa laughs and says he might get along with Iskar Jarak
Night falls, they're in a forest, wolves howl in the distance which makes Karsa smile
Mappo recalls the Battle of Bayen Eckar for no particular reason I can discern
The Trell tribes vs. an army of the Nemil Kingdom. Further west of a Seven Cities
[Note: The Nemil Kingdom is never further explored in any novels]
About 200 years prior to the Malazan series
The Trell tribes were losing a significant amount of its people to the allures of civilization

Three of the four Trell tribe leaders all were comatose when they performed a ritual drinking of a shamananistic concoction granting visions. However the ditch they dug around the cactus had killed and mixed in a toxic spider
It was left to Trynigarr, mocked for his silence because he had no wisdom to share. It was his first battle
For centuries the Trell had began their battles with blind charges, the Nemil general Saylan’mathas had prepared with wall formations of long pikes
The Nemil army confidently strode forward, the Trell too nervous to engage and commit to a charge
Trynigarr, however, had the foresight to send his warriors to surprise slaughter the Nemil supply camp
Trynigarr, having the advantage of knowing the landscape, hid Trell warriors flanking the Nemil’s current position surrounding them
During the battle, the Trell had thrown sacks of black scorpions into the Nemil army, joking that they emptied their yurts for this
Trynigarr led the Trell victoriously against the Nemil this battle, and for six more battles. The Nemil yielded all human claims on Trell lands

In the end, however, Nemil general Saylan’mathas instead chose to slaughter the bhederin that the Trell tribes depended on. The Trell clans all surrendered due to starvation and were driven from their lands. Trynigarr was reduced to a back-alley drunk
[Note: I have no clue the significant of this flashback]
Back to the present, Mappo grows impatient with Iskaral Pust who said they were taking a shortcut through a swamp. What should've taken 2 days turned into 5
Mappo begins to wonder for what reason House Shadow would want to delay him from reuniting with Icarium
Mappo, realizing the ruse, storms off and encounters Spite, a beautiful woman who was formerly a Nameless One cultist that helped release Dejim Nebrahl to kill Mappo
Spite recognized Ardata helped heal Mappo and says she's glad Mappo survived
Spite wants to help Mappo by sharing info about the Nameless Ones as well as supplying him with a ship prepared to pursue their quarry halfway around the world
[Note: Doesn't say what she wants yet or why]
A nine year old that survived Poliel’s plague wakes up several times, eventually able to walk around his village
He is the sole survivor in his village. A dozen wild dogs were fat after eating everyone, including his family
Purple nodes swelled at the bous joints in his arms and legs
Walking north, the boy and the dogs came to a crossroads where a cairn directed them northwards
Felisin Younger watched as the boy and the dogs arrived to the Hanar Ara, the city of the Fallen
[Note: Speculated the Hanar Ara is E’napatha N’apur, the city Icarium had slaughtered far in the past and Heboric’s group passed through before the Unbound attacking them]
Kulat told her that survivors would gather here. The broken, the scarred, the unmanned, and the rare carriers like the boy
Felisin Younger foresees the boy being used as a carrier to spread Poliel's plague to create more survivors for the religion
Hundreds arrived to the city
Herders brought eraga, long limbed cattle thought to have been extinct for thousands of years
Artisans produced images of the Crippled God and his followers on pottery, wall paintings, statues, and fabrics
Kulat observes the nodules of Poliel's plague, or the ‘Many Mouths of the Bluetongue’, are shrinking and the boy will become useless
Felisin Younger for the boy to live in the palace with his dogs in the open wing where Kulat planned to build Felisin Younger’s private garden
Felisin Younger names the boy Crokus

cards.h: Scene 1 (Dujek’s camp outside G’danisban, Ganoes Paran

i.html: Noto Boil stands outside Dujek’s tent, trying to stop Ganoes Paran (pretending to be Cpt. Kindly) from going inside
Noto Boil is a healer from Kartool, worshiper of Soliel, has wispy strands of hair, dark leathery skin, and receding gums that give him a skeletal smile
After some threats, Noto Boil relents and lets Ganoes inside
The first chamber of the tent was filled in haze of d’bayang drug, four commanders lay in cots

In the back was Dujek Onearm, purple blotches around h oh s face, eyes crusted shut with mucus, swollen tongue the color of Aren Steel (blue) forced through his lips, still breathing like a whistle with convulsions
[Note: Dujek led his men into a temple not realizing it belonged to Poliel’s]
Ganoes walked to the outer chamber of the tent and encounters Fist Rythe Bude
Rythe Bude was a dark skinned woman with short wavy hair. A very minor character.
She was from Shal-Morzinn, an isolated empire ruled by Three sorcerer kings for the last thousands of years
[Note: Shal-Morzinn sounds awesome, but sadly also never explored in any Malazan book]
She fled her homeland on a Blue Moranth trader to the Genabarii coast where she signed up in the army and served under Cpt. Kindly
Emperor Kellanved and Dancer had visited Shal-Morzinn on the imperial ship, the Twist. Nothing happened because Shal-Morzinn was powerful but not expansionist

cards.h: Scene 1 (Dujek’s camp outside G’danisban, Ganoes Paran

i.html: Ganoes reveals his true identity and had come to repay a debt to Dujek and keep Poliel from running loose in the mortal realm
Fist Rythe Bude requests a Shal-Morzinn cremation custom, to fill her lungs with oil and burn her body so that her soul would be free
Ganoes leaves the tent
Noto Boil tells Ganoes that outrider Hurlochel was looking for him
Noto Boil recounts a story of Cpt. Kindly hanging a Falah'd, that was a Malazan ally at the time, over a balcony
Ganoes jokes that it was because he was wearing blue and green, which he thought as colours that clash
Ganoes plans to enter Poliel’s temple in G’danisban alone, with Noto Boil to come with him

cards.h: Scene 2 (Dujek’s camp outside G’danisban, Ganoes Paran)

i.html: Outrider Hurlochel pleads with Ganoes to not go through with the plan and lose their company healer
Noto Boil is disavowed from Soliel, has no powers from her
Ganoes mistrusts the gods that claim to be friendly and sympathetic to mortals while leaving true fate to chance is something they have to answer for
Hurlochel noticed Ganoes’s eyes flared like a beast when he said that
Ganoes takes command of the Malaz 5th Army and gives the order to march in four days, an end to the moping and bitching
Doesn't know where to yet, figure it out later
Outrider Hurlochel is happy and gives a sharp salute
As Ganoes and Noto Boil approach G’danisban’s gates, Noti Boil feels the ‘breath of chaos’ and that they'll die if they come closer
Ganoes rides on, Noto Boil feels like the Falah'd that Cpt. Kindly dangled over the balcony

Torahaval Delat reminisces how her younger brother, Adaephon Delat (aka Quick Ben) used to make dolls for all 42 members of their family out of their hair, nails, and teeth to cast nightmares as pranks
They used to live in the Aren, Prelid Quarter
Torahaval chased after Quick Ben one day with one of his wolf dolls. QB foresaw this and placed her underwear inside so when she twisted the wolf doll’s leg she injured herself
Torahaval hated her brother, but as an adult hoped and wished he was still alive
Torahaval Delat is a priestess of Poliel, in the same G’danisban temple that Dujek and his army failed to invade
Bridthok, another priest of Poliel, was trying to categorize the variety of coins discovered the Temple’s coin chest
The chest was bottomless, digging further the coins were nearly frozen
Bridthok believes the coins come from all sorts of realms and cultures
Bridthok was a person that faked his death every year
Torahaval didn't trust the other priests like Septhune Anabhin or Sradal Purthu
Another priest, Sribin, was taken as Poliel’s mortal lover until they rotted away and discarded for another
Bridthok insisted Sha’ik was being reborn with a new cult, Poliel was harvesting a legion for her, and the Crippled God laughs as he manipulates this alliance closer together
Bridthok suddenly stands announcing Poliel has summoned them
Torahaval remembered holding Adaephon Delat as a child from a nightmare, where he was dead yet still walking the world because he had forgotten something
‘How to live’
Fiddler finally brings Bottle to meet Quick Ben and Kalam
Quick Ben has several dolls spread in front of him
Bottle immediately recognizes QB is at an impasse and that one of the dolls is QB’s sister
Apsalar is involved but not in the moment. Was supposed to cross paths with Torahaval, but did not.
Be glad for it [because Apsalar would’ve killed her]
Cotillion’s role was to start the avalanche of events, what happens is up to fate
Shadowthrone is central to everything, but his shadow doesn't reach Torahaval
Bottle picks up the Shadowthrone doll and adjusts it to be on four legs with right arm and left leg raised, but the shadow still doesn't reach Torahaval
Something else with Shadowthrone
Bottle falls asleep
Quick Ben realizes Bottle was half asleep the whole time, the Eres’al (the Tall Ones) was using sympathetic magic to be with Bottle, guiding him
The Eres, a race present before even the K’Chain Che’Malle
Shadowthrone’s doll shadow did not fit the doll
Broad head, prominent and wide snout, jaws open and wrapped around something that slithered like a snake

cards.h: Scene 5, 6 (To Sotka, Apsalar, Telorast and Curdle)

i.html: Apsalar lays on a flat boulder
Listened in on Bottle and Quick Ben’s conversation
Recognized the Ere’sal race and Torahaval’s name being on Mebra’s list, and that both Cotillion and Shadowthrone wanted her dead
Believes Quick Ben now understands the trouble she's in and decided to do something about it
Apsalar gets off the boulder, wields her daggers, shifted into Shadow, and started her Shadow Dance
Telorast and Curdle see Apsalar shifting into Shadow, warning not to mess with her
They know the ‘doom’s come upon them’ and decide to ‘cause trouble’
Quick Ben decides to visit Shadowthrone and casts a ritual with Kalam
Kalam stabs a knife into the sand, Quick Ben scolds him to use a non-otataral dagger
Quick Ben pulls out a doll with long strands and ties those strands around the knife
Quick Ben sits down, legs crossed, and ties his soul to the doll
As soon as the strings are taut, Kalam needs to pull the dagger
Fiddler has a bad feeling, which is what he's known for and is always right. Like an omen, Kalam gets even more nervous
[Note: Previous bad feeling was during the Siege of Pale when the Bridgeburners almost all died. Fiddler’s warning saved their lives]
Ganoes carves a magical arch and a pattern onto G’danisban’s city wall, allowing him and Noto Boil to move through the wall into the city
Noto Boil says he's disavowed because he couldn't agree to the life of a corrupt priest
Ganoes say he heard Noto Boil lost a power struggle in Kartool concerning the temple treasury
Noto Boil senses Poliel’s poison in the air
A naked girl approaches Ganoes and Noto Boil, the same girl that Fiddler, Crokus, and Apsalar rescued when they visited G’danisban during the Whirlwind Rebellion
[Note: Not the grandchildren of Kimloc, the Tanno Spiritwalker]
Noto Boil senses she is a Chosen of Soliel
Soliel’s chosen warns that Brokeface and his hunters are coming, Ganoes plans to meet them and force a meeting with Poliel
Brokeface hates horses
Ganoes orders Noto Boil to go with Soliel’s chosen and meet up at the Grand Temple later
Paran also expects an offer from Soliel which he won't take no for an answer
Noto Boil apologizes to Soliel through her chosen for Ganoes’ disrespect and would be on her side if she chose to smite Ganoes
Soliel speaks through her chosen with an older voice, telling him to shut up and that the entire world is depending on him. She does not want to be known as the goddess that fucked everything up
Soliel’s chosen says her only desire now is to witness and runs off. Noto Boil chases after her
Ganoes rides down the main avenue and encounters a mob led by Brokeface, whose face had been bitten and ruined by a horse
Brokeface senses Ganoes is unaffected by Poliel, that there is a beast in his eyes
Ganoes convinces Brokeface to lead him to Poliel
Torahaval spent her life drifting from one temple’s faith to another
She’s learned one god can be misshapen into multiple faces to fit whatever the worshipers wanted
The kindest gods have the most violent worshipers because of their extremist views, killing and staining their hands with blood
Torahaval had been a violent worshiper
Torahaval joined Poliel’s faith fourteen months ago in Karashimesh, diving deeper despite knowing she should be hurt
Poliel is the Crippled God’s poisoned lover
Torahaval and Bridthok walked to Poliel’s altar, where Septhune Anabhin of Omari and Sradal Purthu waits for Poliel to choose a new mortal lover after Sribin died
Poliel’s invisible hand with countless fingers grabbed Torahaval and pulled her closer, the priests were more relieved than pitying of her
A rider on a horse storms into the temple and Torahaval drops to the ground, grateful to her savior
The rider is Ganoes Paran, he asks ‘What ails them?’
Brokeface thinks that was hilarious, but also angry that Gamoes dares ride his horse into the temple
'Can't you feel her wrath? Her outrage? Oh, you foolish man!’
‘Can she feel mine?’
Ganoes approaches Poliel sitting on her throne of bones on the altar

Long limbs with oozing with infection and venom, a bare flat chest that appeared androgynous, multi-jointed legs with three talons for toes, black bowls for eyes with the faintest spark, lips broad, cracked, and oozing
Poliel doesn't know what Ganoes is, senses he's a Soletaken (Hound form)
‘The truth behind the veil. Blood was their [her worshipers’] path. And so we choose to poison it’
Ganoes tosses an otataral shard for her to catch
Instead, it pierced Poliel’s hand and sends her into an agonizing convulsion. Chaotic power, unleashed, waves of gray fire pulsed, tiles exploded
Ganoes wonders if he shouldn’t have done that
Ganoes looks down at Torahaval and sees her shadow fragmented and slashed
Quick Ben enters the Shadow Warren, meeting Shadowthrone on his.. Shadow throne to try and spare his sister
Torahaval had tried several rituals to break her her ties to Quick Ben, but Quick Ben made sure his threads were invincible
Shadowthrone says even he doesn't have the power to save her from Poliel
Quick Ben is surprised to learn about Poliel, but insists that Bottle stated Shadowthrone is involved somehow
Shadowthrone forces Quick Ben to accept his past debt, Quick Ben accepts and is sent away
Shadowthrone conjured a small farm scythe in his hand and cuts away at the threads
Kalam grabs Bottle by the neck, the threads were cut clean, Kalam and Fiddler demand Bottle go after Quick Ben
Bottle sees Apsalar in the distance wondering what she’s doing, Kalam and Fiddler run after her
Hurlochel, Cpt. Sweetcreek, and Cpl. Futhgar were outside when the Hounds of Shadow were charging through the camp, knocking people in the air as they ran into the walls of G’danisban
Hurlochel saw fear in the Hounds’ eyes
Five more, bigger hounds were coming
[Note: Deragoth]

cards.h: Scene 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 (Poliel’s Temple, Noto Boil, Ganoes, Brokeface)

i.html: Noto Boil’s horse suddenly runs away, kicking Noto Boil off its back
Noto Boil lands, cracking ribs, and his fish spine that he chews on gets lodged in his throat
Soliel’s chosen pulls out the spine for him
Poliel writhed as Ganoes’ otataral shard pinned her to the mortal realm
Ganoes clarifies he isn't a Soletaken at all, but Hurlochel’s comment on his eyes was closer to the truth
Ganoes sees Torahaval’s body on the ground and thinks the Hounds won't touch her
Ganoes leaves with this final message, ‘Mess with mortals, Poliel, and you pay’
Brokeface felt alone and helpless as the priests of Poliel fled and Poliel was dying. He is a broken man.
Quick Ben appears right between Poliel and Torahaval, his sister
The Hounds’ howls are heard in the distance
Ganoes leaves Poliel’s Temple as he dodges on his horse as the Hounds Shan, Rood, Baran carrying Dejim Nebrahl in his mouth, Blind, and Gear ran into the temple
Ganoes tells Noto Boil to get up and for Soliel [through her chosen] to direct them to her temple
Soliel states her sister is dying
Ganoes sees the first of the Deragoth
Quick Ben grabs his sister but feels trapped in a room with otataral and the Hounds inside
Ready to die, Brokeface walked into the Hound’s path but is tackled out of the way by Apsalar
Apsalar cut through the Hounds and kicked one with enough force to send it airborne and crash into the wall
Telorast and Curdle flanked Apsalar, hissing at the Hounds, and the Hound were afraid of them
Apsalar tells Brokeface to follow Quick Ben through a bolt-hole emergency exit behind the dais, Brokeface tells her he just wants to die
That statement was enough to make Apsalar take her eyes off of the Hounds, face him, and look at him not with judgment, but sorrow
She insists instead that he follow Ganoes to Soliel’s temple, who no longer turns away with Ganoes at her throat
‘Go. Be healed.’
The Deragoth come closer, the Hounds bunch closer together more desperately, and Brokeface runs into the emergency exit
Quick Ben runs down the tunnel with Torahaval over his shoulders, Brokeface catches up and helps him carry his sister

cards.h: Scene 24, 25, 26 (Poliel’s Temple, Apsalar, Poliel, Quick Ben)

i.html: Apsalar leaves as Telorast and Curdle has less effect at holding the Hounds back, they want to stay but follow after Apsalar
Poliel was suffering, trapped on her throne by the otataral shard
The Crippled God’s power left her, wondered for whose sake and liberation was Ganoes fighting for
Poliel’s purpose and wish of her worshippers was to end mortal life that was destroying and polluting the world. To save and heal the goddess Burn.
‘Only humans centre salvation solely upon themselves’
[Note: This answers the question, out of all the cool gods to choose from why tf would anyone worship disease? Turns out it was environmentalists]
The Hounds entered the chamber and dropped Dejim Nebrahl at her feet
[Note: You can assume Dejim Nebrahl dies here]
The Deragoth, the first enslavers of humanity, arrived
Brokeface recognizes that Torahaval is inflicted by Bluetongue, his goddess Poliel's plague and that they should go to Soliel’s temple
Quick Ben calls Soliel an indifferent bitch, Brokeface insists to trust her [Apsalar]
Quick Ben agrees with Brokeface
A shriek from Poliel’s temple quakes the tunnel
Ganoes kicks down the doors to Soliel’s temple, entering and tossing Noto Boil on the floor, tosses down a card to summon Soliel
Hopes Poliel’s temple collapsing also kills the Deragoth
Soliel leaves her chosen’s body and appears before Ganoes. Adrogynous with long fingers
Soliel says Ganoes is making a mistake and understands nothing
Ganoes orders her to heal everyone and end Seven Cities’ suffering
Soliel relents, placing the burden of suffering on Ganoes
Quick Ben and Brokeface enters the temple to drop off Torahaval
Ganoes remembers seeing Torahaval on the floor and realizes he knows nothing and everything may have been orchestrated
Because of Quick Ben and Ganoes’ deals with Shadowthrone, Soliel screams that her sister is being torn apart by the Deragoth
Quick Ben asks Ganoes of they can trust his sister Tavore
Ganoes says Tavore sees no difference between herself and her soldiers [Note: vague yes]
Quick Ben says he owes Ganoes a drink after it's all over leaves before his sister wakes up and suffers her wrath, Ganoes would understand having a scary sister himself
Torahaval wakes up, saying she met the sweetest wolf in the world
[Note: Quick Ben and his wolf dolls in their childhood]
Quick Ben wakes up next to Bottle, back with the other Malazans
Kalam and Fiddler assumed by the blood on her daggers, Apsalar had tried to kill QB. She is unarmed and has an expression of resignation
Quick Ben rushes over to stop them, thanks Apsalar for saving them and sparing his sister, and realizes Apsalar is suicidal
Cpt. Faradan Sort appears, saying they're about to march and Sinn thinks they'll reach the rest of the Malaz 14th Army that night
The Hounds lay around at Shadowthrone’s feet, exhausted and injured from Apsalar
ST blames Cotillion for Quick Ben escaping
Cotillion tries to pet the Hounds but they growl at him. He whines that it wasn't his fault but they don't look convinced
Ganoes and Noto Boil return to the Malaz 5th Army outside G’danisban
Noto Boil accuses Ganoes of deception, that brother and sister now lead the Malazan armies on Seven Cities. At least until Dujek gets up
Hurlochel was unable to speak
Cpt. Sweetcreek informs Ganoes that Dujek died two hours ago, all officers ordered to read Dujek’s logs, knows who Ganoes really is, and unanimously voted Ganoes to be the next High Fist
Ganoes remembers Soliel’s words
‘As for suffering, I leave that to you, and through no choice of mine’
Everything Ganoes had done was already far too late
The Malaz 14th Army are on the northern coastline
Fears of mutiny and dwindling supplies will all cities to the west fallen to plague
The heart of the 14th Army, the veterans, had died in Y’Ghatan. Now the army rots from the inside
Fist Tene Baralta, crippled and disfigured, wants to die and only spews out poisonous words when he speaks
Fist Keneb sees Nether leave the command tent with Bent and Roach
The Adjunct is not happy that Nether has lost contact with Dujek since before Y’Ghatan and has no way to track the Claw, Pearl, who vanished
Keneb warns that constant frowning on her young face is going to develop wrinkles, Nether walks off
Fist Keneb enters the command tent. Adjunct Tavore, Fist Blistig, and Admiral Nok are in discussion
Admiral Nok relays that Empress Laseen wants the Malaz 14th Army to return to the capital Unta
The challenge is the route. The western path takes them through mapped territories, but that also takes them through all the cities that are plagued.
Nowhere to resupply
The easter path circumnavigates the rest of the Seven Cities continents through Sepik, Nemil, and Shal-Morzinn who are not certain to trade with Malazans
Blistig hopes they won't have to force the cities to trade by force, which unintentionally shows his lack of confidence in Adjunct Tavore as a leader
Admiral Nok reports of ships he doesn't recognize. Either from raiders from a floating Meckros city or Nemil guard ships
Admiral Nok leaves
Adjunct Tavore orders Fist Blistig to relay the orders to Fist Tene Baralta
Adjunct Tavore shares with Fist Keneb her thoughts on the army’s future
Believes Empress Laseen might send them to Korel and assault the island of Theft
Keneb could tell that even Tavore doesn't believe that
Fist Keneb is dismissed and he finds Grub outside with Bent and Roach
Grub says they need to wait for three days until they can leave. Not two days or they'll die
Grun says Sepik will be bad, Nemil will first be good then be bad, find friends twice, and end up back where they started [Note: Aren] which is very bad
Big man with cut hands says yes
Grub runs off with his bone whistle and the two dogs to collect seashells
Lt. Pores walks in on the heavy infantry collecting and drilling holes in bones to wear, Pores takes some for himself
When reaching Cpt. Kindly, he coughs and drops the bones, saying he's losing some every time he coughs
Cpt. Kindly has laid out his collection of combs throughout his life as a soldier, strange because he is bald
Rants about how he would've led the Malazan Army better
The other soldiers would prefer Kindly’s straightforward leadership because at least they won't be kept in the dark about the leader’s secret plans
Lt. Pores believes times have changed, since Kellanved and Dassem Ultor had trained their soldiers to be able to think for themselves
Barathol gets the mules and Heboric’s corpse ready to go as Crokus and Scillara hand over her baby to the two Jessa’s
Chaur comes with his own pack
Already accepting that he can't convince Chaur to stay home, Barathol gives Chaur his shoes so Chaur doesn't have to walk barefoot
Crokus is comforted by Barathol’s presence especially after seeing how he treats Chaur
Crokus plans on taking Heboric’s corpse to the Jade statue on otataral isle, was Heboric’s last mission
Crokus checked his corpse and found that Heboric’s hands are now a solid jade
His body was mummified to preserve it and prevent maggots
Scillara wants to follow Crokus and become a thief like him in Darujhistan, Crokus suggests she might get along with Coll or Murillio better
Scillara wonders if she just got insulted
Barathol jokes he's like an animal being led to slaughter
Scillara could tell Crokus is depressed from failing his mission in protecting Heboric, Felisin Younger, and Scillara as well as losing the girl [Apsalar] he left Darujhistan in the first place
Scillara was looking forward to starting a new life in Darujhistan with new friends, new adventure, and Crokus
Scillara tried to pester Barathol and Crokus with questions, their terse responses amused her and she seems to be enjoying herself
Chaur trails behind, still smiling
Ganath arrives at the skykeep that she had trapped in Omtose Phellack sorcery
[Note: Probably the same one that Mappo and Icarium visited]
Senses draconian blood [Sorrit, slain] and the warren of Chaos used to devour her sorcery
Wishes fellow Jaghut, Cynnigig or Phyrlis, or even the human Ganoes, was there to keep her company
K’Chain Nah’Ruk appear, the Short Tails, appear and kill Ganath ☠
Mappo, Spite, and Iskaral Pust reach the northern coastline where a crew of Iskaral's bhok'arala waited with a caravel ship they most likely stole
Spite senses a murder [Note: Ganath] and ‘godless ones’ are on Seven Cities again

Spite discusses how the war of the gods is not direct slinging of thunderbolts and earthquakes, but fanatics engaged with battle lines unclear and not knowing what weapons are effective. Some that may even harm themselves
The root of fanaticism is inequity. When one side is far too rich, the poor will understand they will never attain what the rich have and rise up, civilization falls and anarchy prevails
When inequity leads to violence, the gods become helpless and the morals they stood for are the first victims
‘All that they do in that god’s name is at its core profoundly godless’
Spite connects her discussion to Icarium
When Icarium is sane, he fights against inequality and injustice
When Icarium loses control, he doesn't fight for anything. He simply annihilates
Spite believes motivation becomes irrelevant. Slaughter is slaughter
Inequity ends when no one and nothing is left standing. That is the Nameless One’s purpose for Icarium
Spite speaks of two kingdoms, one upriver and one downriver
The upper kingdom struggles with irrigation as the topsoil is swept away
The lower kingdom receives foul water and sewage
The kingdoms argue, go to war, destroy the land, and the lower kingdom is victorious
However, the upper kingdom’s irrigation is destroyed resulting in floods that destroy the lower kingdom
Despite the lower kingdom having a valid reason to fight, the valid reason does nothing to defend the lower kingdom against its own annihilation
Civilizations choose the easiest enemy to blame, when the true enemy are all the things that destroy in the long term
Overhunting into extinction, deforestation, farming, irrigation, waste production, disease
However, leaders who make a platform to fight against those long term enemies are destroyed by the wealthy whose wealth becomes threatened
The wealthy the choose an enemy and place blame on them
Spite considers Mappo’s Trell people to be successful pastoralists and bhederin herders, but were doomed by those who coveted the Trell’s land for its wealth
Iskaral mocks their philosophical discussion, Mappo points out Iskaral is the bhok'arala’s god and they mimic pulling at their hair
A dome barrow of limestone slabs and brick was built for Dujek Onearm’s burial
The toad, Gumble, watched as the Malazan imperial artist Ormulogun mixed his paints with weird shit
Gumble accuses Ormulogun of having propaganda in his art for heroic deeds of the deed, but as a result people don't have faith in those still alive
Gumble sees the sketches Ormulgan planned to paint inside the three walls of the barrow
Dujek at shattered gates of Black Coral
Dujek at the parley with Caladan Brood and Anomander Rake
Dujek and Tayschrenn outside Pale before the siege
Ganoes look at his High Fist’s armor, feeling impostor syndrome but doesn't want to read what Dujek wrote about him
Thinks Dujek wanted to elevate House Paran so that people would have more faith in Tavore’s command of the Malaz 14th Army
Ganoes says he'll do whatever he wants until Laseen learns about the field promotion and fire him
Hurlochel enters the tent, saying the Fists and entire army have been standing at attention for awhile and they're weak
Ganoes forgoes the armor and wonders why they follow him
Hurlochel points out that Ganoes took a single healer into the temple that killed Dujek, struck down the goddess Poliel, and forced the goddess Soliel to give powers of healing to a dozen soldiers
Fist Ruthe Bude reports they have enough supplies for a six to seven day march
Hurlochel reports G’danisban’s surviving population is making a pilgrimage towards the northeast direction

Ganoes orders to delay the march two days so that the army can take what they can get from G'danisban's stores without starving the remaining that still lie in the city and that they'll follow the pilgrimage.
Also to extend invitation to the citizens to join the Malazan train
Dismisses the meeting
Soliel’s former chosen, Naval D’natha, seems to be standing behind Hurlochel as apart of Ganoes’ entourage
Ganos heads to find Ormulogun so he could paint a new Deck of Dragons
Samar Dev, Karsa, and Boatfinder find the body of an Anibar tribesman, Stonefinder
Karsa investigates the tracks and concludes Stonefinder was toyed with before being killed, and that the enemy had taken prisoners
Karsa runs off head towards the enemy, Samar Dev runs after him
When she catched up, Karsa slaughtered his way into the middle of ~50 Tiste Edur
Karsa swung his sword, sending three Tiste Edur flying, one falling and knocking down two others
Karsa dodges six spear and axe attacks, swings to decapitate one and chops down to cut off another’s arm
Karsa uses his left hand to pull one by his spear and grab his neck, crushing it, fluid bursting from eyes, nose, and mouth
At the same time, Karsa’s right sword arm swings up to block several weapons, then chops down through one’s ribs, hid heart dangli by arteries and still beating
Feather Witch is present as the blonde women casting spells from the Tiste Edur canoes, no effect
Samar Dev warns Karsa to stop because more of the enemies will come and more Anibar will die
Karsa points to the Anibar, strapped face down naked on wooden frames being cooked alive over coal embers
The Tiste Edur brings out their interpreter, a man Samar Dev refers to as ‘the Taxilian’ because of his arm tattoos
[Note: Taxila is a city on the peninsula directly north of Y’Ghatan]
Samar Dev wants Karsa to lie that he is the first of many to scare them away
Karsa says ‘If they leave I cannot kill more of them’
The Preda [Hanradi Khalag] and Feather Witch argue, Taxilian listens to them and winks at Samar Dev

[Note: Hanradi Khalag of the Merude tribe. They were the only tribe of the Tiste Edur six that opposed the Warlock King’s attempt to unify the tribes.
